title: ALGORITHMS FOR REDUCING THE TIME REQUIRED TO PERFORM OPERATIONS OF THE DOMINGO-FERRER CRYPTOSYSTEM
abstract: Проведён анализ литературы по тематике полностью гомоморфного шифрования. Представлено краткое описание полностью гомоморфной криптографической системы Доминго-Феррера, основанной на задаче факторизации чисел, приведены временные характеристики этапов атаки с известным открытым текстом на данную криптосистему. Проанализированы временные характеристики операций криптосистемы, описаны методы и средства их практической реализации. Предложены новые алгоритмы реализации операций криптосистемы Доминго-Феррера, позволяющие снизить время их выполнения. Обоснование оценок временных затрат операций криптосистемы формируется на основе теоретических расчётов, а также результатов экспериментальных исследований. Целью исследования является снижение времени выполнения операций криптосистемы Доминго-Феррера посредством разработки алгоритмов их модификации, учитывающих особенности практической реализации. Основным результатом настоящей работы является снижение времени выполнения следующих операций криптосистемы Доминго-Феррера: шифрования – на 10-15%, расшифрования – в 2 раза, гомоморфного умножения – в 64 раза для цепочки из 200 умножений при использовании степени полиномов представления шифртекста d=100 и незначительном увеличении временных затрат на генерацию ключа. title: AI ‐Augmented Memory and Consumer Sustainability: Understanding Dual Consumption Pathways in Digital Retail
abstract: ABSTRACT In digital retail, algorithmic personalisation shapes consumer outcomes, yet the cognitive mechanisms involved in this process remain theoretically underspecified. This paper introduces AI‐augmented memory (AI‐AM), a mechanism that algorithms use to record, retrieve and resurface prior behavioural traces during consumer decision‐making. The study draws on 30 semi‐structured interviews with Singapore‐based e‐commerce consumers and a complementary practitioner‐reflexive account by the researcher, based on over 10 years of multi‐platform retail experience. It examines how AI‐AM both enables and undermines SDG12 (responsible consumption and production). The thematic analysis identifies a dual pathway: a sustainable pathway, where AI‐AM reduces trial‐and‐error purchasing and supports deliberative restraint and an unsustainable pathway, where the same mechanism amplifies impulse purchase loops and erodes autonomous restraint. Four contextual conditions were associated with pathway activation: a pragmatic need‐based norm, platform‐mediated social proof, age‐associated variation in pathway responses and reliance on AI recommendations. The study extends the Engel–Kollat–Blackwell (EKB) model by theorising AI‐AM as a recursive dual‐pathway sustainability gate and develops a sustainability‐aligned design typology for platform designers and policymakers.

title: Dicke superposition probes for noise-resilient Heisenberg and super-Heisenberg metrology
abstract: Phase sensing with entangled multi-qubit states in the presence of noise is a central theme of modern quantum metrology. The present work investigates Dicke state superposition probes for quantum phase sensing under parameter encoding generated by one- and two-body interaction Hamiltonians. Under linear collective-spin encoding, near-optimal Dicke superposition states are shown to exhibit significantly enhanced robustness against phase damping noise compared with Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ), W-superposition, and balanced Dicke states, while maintaining favorable metrological performance under realistic decoherence channels. For two-body interactions, optimal probe states maximizing the quantum Fisher information are identified. Their noise resilience and metrological scaling behaviour under phase damping, amplitude damping, and global depolarizing channels are analyzed. The associated near-optimal Dicke superposition states are found to exhibit improved resilience to phase damping, for the system sizes considered. These results establish tailored near-optimal Dicke state superposition probes as versatile and noise-resilient resources for Heisenberg and super-Heisenberg quantum phase sensing governed by one- and two-body interactions.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge: Concerning Rubric Artifacts in LLM-based Automated Text Generation Evaluation
abstract: LLM-as-a-Judge pipelines are increasingly used to evaluate AI-generated text, based on the assumption that judgments arise from reasoning over candidate responses with respect to a rubric. We show that this assumption warrants further scrutiny. Classifiers trained only on rubric text, without access to any evaluated response, achieve nontrivial predictive performance on judge outputs. This suggests that rubric formulations encode recoverable evaluative signals, allowing scores to be partially anticipated independently of model outputs. Finally, counterfactual perturbations reveal that judges often fail to reliably update their decisions when either the candidate response or the rubric criterion is reversed. Our findings raise concerns about the reliability of rubric-based LLM evaluation and highlight the need for further methodological study of automated evaluation via LLMs.

title: Can LLMs Use Relational Transformer Embeddings?
abstract: Injecting frozen relational-encoder embeddings as soft tokens into a large language model (LLM) is a conceptually appealing fusion strategy: the encoder handles multi-table structure, the LLM handles language and reasoning, and no lossy text serialization is required. We test this hypothesis concretely by injecting embeddings from a frozen Relational Transformer (RT) into Qwen3.5-4B via a learned MLP projection and LoRA adaptation, trained first with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on chain-of-thought reasoning traces and then with group-based reinforcement learning (GSPO). We evaluate across 10 binary classification tasks on 6 relational databases from RelBench, under four supervision regimes: single-task (ST), within-dataset (WD), cross-dataset (CD), and all-task (ALL). The hybrid model does not consistently outperform standalone RT: it is frequently below random, highly sensitive to serialization format and relational-token budget, and unstable under RL training. We report these negative results and analyze the failure modes, arguing that soft-token fusion requires stronger alignment objectives and schema-aware design before it can serve as a reliable route to relational prediction.

title: DASC: Decay-Aware State Compression for Hybrid Linear-Attention Serving
abstract: Hybrid linear-attention architectures have recently scaled to large open-weight models, offering quality competitive with full attention while substantially reducing key/value (KV) cache growth. However, their in-place recurrent-state updates complicate cache management: prefix reuse requires state checkpoints alongside full-attention KV, while storing state checkpoints in full increases memory pressure, leading to more evictions and repeated prefill. By analyzing the decay structure of Gated DeltaNet (GDN) and Kimi Delta Attention (KDA), we find that different heads and channels retain prefix information over markedly different timescales, which we term \emph{retention horizons}. This variation suggests substantial compression potential in persistent state checkpoints. Building on this observation, we introduce \emph{Decay-Aware State Compression} (DASC), which derives retention horizons from model weights, selects long-horizon state units, and packs them into a ragged state checkpoint layout. To integrate efficiently with tensor-parallel inference engines, DASC furtherly balances compressed state checkpoints across TP ranks. On reuse, DASC either zero-fills omitted units or refreshes them from a bounded suffix with additional compute cost. Across retrieval and end-to-end reasoning benchmarks on Kimi-Linear, conservative DASC configurations remain close to full caching while compressing KDA recurrent state checkpoints by $2.63\times$. Under fixed state checkpoint memory budgets, the resulting capacity gains reduce mean Time to First Token (TTFT) by 42.6\% and improve input throughput by 68.4\%. At larger compression ratio, suffix refresh recovers much of the accuracy lost to more aggressive omission, at the cost of additional replay computation. Qwen with GDN exhibits a similar quality--efficiency trend, showing that DASC extends from channel-wise KDA to head-wise GDN.

title: Photovoltaic Power Output Prediction Using PCA–KNN: A Comparative Study with SVR and MLP on Historical Operational Data
abstract: The transition toward renewable energy integration in power systems presents challenges in managing photovoltaic (PV) power output owing to variations in operating conditions. This study evaluated the performance of K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), with and without Principal Component Analysis (PCA), for PV power output prediction. The dataset comprised 420 observations recorded at five-minute intervals over seven days of measurements from a PV system. The data were chronologically divided into 80% training and 20% testing sets, while normalization and PCA were exclusively fitted to the training data to prevent information leakage. The model performance was evaluated using the Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and coefficient of determination (R²). The results show that KNN and PCA-KNN achieved the best and identical performance, with an MSE of 265.3385, RMSE of 16.2892, and R² of 0.8421. PCA did not improve KNN accuracy but maintained its predictive performance after the dimensional transformation. PCA-MLP showed a slight improvement over MLP, whereas SVR and PCA-SVR yielded lower performances. These findings indicate that the effect of PCA depends on both the dataset characteristics and the learning algorithm. Further studies with longer observation periods, more diverse datasets, and external validation are recommended to assess the generalizability of the models.

title: Data for "Structured Representations and Outcome-Conditioned Output Matching in a Large Language Model"
abstract: This dataset provides the frozen research data underlying the study “Structured Representations and Outcome-Conditioned Output Matching in a Large Language Model.” It includes the fixed stimulus set, model-generated interpretations, primary and repeat judgments, analysis-unit data, stimulus-level outcome-assimilation results, frozen secondary endpoint results, and source data underlying the reported figures and tables. The deposited materials correspond to the frozen analysis reported in the manuscript and are provided to support transparency and reproducibility.

title: 弦-复共轭的量子纠缠扩展计算
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement expansion computation framework centered on the unique properties of the弦-复共轭 (弦-复) system. We propose a new quantum measurement algorithm leveraging the inherent correlations between entangled particles, aiming to surpass the limitations of classical computation. The core mechanism involves transforming the quantum entanglement process into a specialized quantum measurement algorithm that significantly expands the potential range and capabilities of quantum information processing. This work demonstrates the potential of this approach to unlock new computational paradigms and offers a distinct pathway for future quantum computing advancements. We present a preliminary implementation of the proposed algorithm and discuss its theoretical implications.

title: Symbolic Regression with Quantum Annealing
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, the exponential growth in the solution space with increasing data complexity often presents a significant challenge. This paper investigates the potential of quantum annealing to accelerate symbolic regression. We propose a framework where a quantum annealing algorithm is directly employed to search for symbolic expressions that accurately represent the underlying relationship between input and output variables. The core idea is to leverage the quantum tunneling effect to efficiently navigate the complex, multi-modal cost function associated with symbolic regression, thereby escaping local minima and identifying optimal symbolic solutions more quickly. We demonstrate that quantum annealing can offer a viable approach to tackling this problem, particularly for datasets with moderate complexity. The approach's effectiveness stems from its ability to explore a vast solution space in parallel, a capability inherent to quantum computation. The results suggest that quantum annealing provides a novel and potentially significant enhancement to traditional symbolic regression methods.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Probabilistic Logic Programming
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neuro-symbolic programming that leverages the strengths of both neural networks and probabilistic logic programming. The core idea is to utilize neural networks to learn and generate logical rules, which are then executed within a probabilistic logic programming engine for reasoning and inference. This framework offers a more robust and interpretable solution for neuro-symbolic integration compared to traditional methods, by anchoring symbolic reasoning within a probabilistic framework. We present a detailed description of the architecture, including the neural rule generator and the probabilistic logic programming engine, and outline the key mechanisms for rule learning and execution. The approach addresses the challenges of brittle rule learning and lack of interpretability often associated with purely symbolic systems, while mitigating the instability and limited reasoning capabilities of conventional neural networks. Ultimately, this work demonstrates the potential for creating intelligent systems that seamlessly combine the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the logical deduction abilities of probabilistic logic programming.

title: Explainable Graph Neural Networks for Causal Inference
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to graph neural networks (GNNs) that integrates causal inference capabilities, addressing the long-standing "black box" problem inherent in traditional GNNs. The core idea is to develop explainable GNN models capable of discerning causal relationships between nodes within a graph, moving beyond mere correlation. The primary contribution lies in providing a structured method for incorporating causal reasoning into GNNs, significantly enhancing their utility in domains requiring nuanced understanding of interdependencies. Our approach offers a pathway toward building truly intelligent and trustworthy GNN systems.

title: Bio-Inspired Neural Architecture Optimization via Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural architecture optimization (NAO) inspired by biological neural networks. Traditional NAO methods primarily rely on mathematical optimization techniques, often neglecting the intricacies of biological neuron dynamics and adaptation. We propose a simulation-based framework that mimics the learning and adaptive behavior of biological neurons within complex environments. This framework utilizes a detailed, biologically plausible neuron model incorporating synaptic plasticity, neuronal communication, and noise adaptation, coupled with reinforcement learning to iteratively optimize the neural architecture. The core claim is that by simulating the learning and adaptation processes observed in biological neurons, we can design more robust and adaptive neural architectures. The key mechanism involves building a biologically accurate neuron model, simulating key biological processes, and applying reinforcement learning for optimization. The results demonstrate the potential of this approach to generate architectures exhibiting superior performance compared to those obtained through purely mathematical optimization.

title: Graph-Based Anomaly Detection Using Learned Temporal Graph Embeddings
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of anomaly detection in graph data, particularly where temporal dependencies are crucial. Traditional anomaly detection methods often fail to effectively capture the dynamic nature of graphs, resulting in missed anomalies. We propose a novel approach that leverages learned temporal graph embeddings to represent the evolution of graph structure over time. These embeddings are then used as input to graph-based anomaly detection techniques, such as graph autoencoders, allowing for the identification of anomalous patterns that would otherwise be difficult to detect. The core contribution lies in the combination of graph embedding learning with temporal anomaly detection, providing a more robust and accurate method for identifying deviations from normal behavior within dynamic graph systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a conceptual framework.

title: Bismarck Giant Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bismarck Giant Rat
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Bismarck Giant Rat (BGR), inspired by the unique foraging behavior of the Bismarck Giant Rat, a large, robust rodent known for its efficient food search strategies in challenging environments. BGR leverages the rat's adaptive movement patterns, particularly its ability to explore diverse areas while maintaining a focus on promising regions, to develop a robust and effective optimization process. The algorithm incorporates key features of the rat's behavior, including a weighted exploration-exploitation strategy, a dynamic adjustment of search radius based on local food density, and a mechanism for escaping local optima. We detail the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and theoretical analysis. The performance of BGR is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The results show BGR's efficiency and adaptability in solving complex optimization problems.

title: Bicolored Shrew Optimization Algorithm (BSOA): A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Uropsilus rutilus*
abstract: This paper presents the Bicolored Shrew Optimization Algorithm (BSOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Uropsilus rutilus*, a small shrew species known for its unique and efficient foraging strategy. The algorithm mimics the shrew's ability to rapidly search for food sources by utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation phases, guided by a novel adaptive inertia weight mechanism and a dynamic probability distribution. The BSOA incorporates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) to achieve robust performance in a variety of optimization problems. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the core mechanics of the algorithm, including the position update equation, the velocity update equation, and the probability calculation for food source selection. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of BSOA in solving benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's key innovations lie in its adaptive inertia weight control and the dynamic probability distribution, which contribute to its ability to escape local optima and converge to global solutions efficiently. Future research will focus on further refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability to complex real-world problems.

title: Title: Universal Quantum State Transfer Protocol for Information Transfer
abstract: Quantum information transfer presents significant challenges due to the fragility of quantum states and the potential for decoherence. Traditional quantum communication methods, reliant on complex quantum repeaters, are limited in their reach and require substantial resources. This paper introduces a novel quantum state transfer protocol, dubbed the "Universal Quantum State Transfer Protocol," designed to overcome these limitations by leveraging entanglement swapping to enable efficient and robust state transfer across any distance, minimizing decoherence and error. The protocol's core principle centers around rapid and lossless state transfers, drastically reducing the need for complex quantum repeaters. This work explores the implementation of a unique entanglement swapping mechanism to achieve this goal, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize quantum communication. The resulting protocol offers a pathway towards more practical and scalable quantum communication systems.

This is achieved through a framework integrating entangled state generation, quantum decoy-state protocol for key distribution, and an entanglement resource optimization algorithm. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the entanglement generation and utilization based on real-time feedback, mitigating the impact of noise and interference. We demonstrate, theoretically, how this adaptive approach can significantly improve information transmission efficiency and security compared to traditional, static encoding methods within Quantum Key Distribution (QKD). The key innovation lies in harnessing the dynamic nature of entanglement, providing enhanced robustness against channel impairments. The theoretical framework outlines a robust mechanism for achieving optimal performance in QKD scenarios. ---

title: Probabilistic Programming for Simulating Complex Systems with Uncertainty
abstract: This paper explores the application of probabilistic programming languages (PPLs) for simulating complex systems characterized by inherent uncertainty. Traditional simulation methods often require significant manual effort in defining stochastic elements, handling uncertainty, and performing Bayesian inference. PPLs offer a more declarative approach, allowing users to specify the underlying probabilistic model directly, facilitating automated inference and sensitivity analysis. We argue that PPLs provide a more intuitive and efficient workflow for modeling and simulating complex systems, leading to improved understanding and decision-making in the face of uncertainty. The core mechanism involves defining a simulation model within a PPL, incorporating stochastic elements and leveraging the language's built-in support for Bayesian inference. This approach simplifies the entire simulation process, reducing the need for manual intervention and enabling more robust and reliable results. We demonstrate this principle through a conceptual framework and highlight the advantages of using PPLs for complex system simulation.

title: Ansell's Wood Mouse: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Apodemus sylvaticus*
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Ansell's Wood Mouse" (AWM), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in *Apodemus sylvaticus*, commonly known as the wood mouse. Wood mice exhibit remarkable adaptability and efficiency in locating and exploiting food resources within their environment. AWM leverages these observed behaviors – specifically, the combination of exploratory and exploitative movements, coupled with a dynamic adjustment of search radius – to construct a robust and effective optimization algorithm. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a novel mutation operator designed to mimic the erratic, yet purposeful, movements of the wood mouse during its foraging expeditions. We demonstrate the algorithm's performance across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to effectively navigate complex search spaces and achieve competitive results compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization. The core of AWM is the "Radius Adjustment Mechanism" (RAM), which dynamically scales the search radius based on the current population's convergence rate. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be relatively insensitive to specific problem instances, offering a degree of robustness. We provide a detailed description of the algorithm's design, its underlying principles, and a comparative analysis of its performance against other metaheuristic techniques. The results suggest that AWM holds significant promise as a versatile optimization tool, particularly in scenarios requiring adaptability and efficient exploration.

title: Dynamic Programming for Quantum Circuit Compilation with Uncertainty
abstract: Quantum circuit compilation is a critical step in the process of translating high-level quantum algorithms into executable instructions on quantum hardware. Traditional compilation techniques often rely on deterministic models of gate operations and measurement outcomes, which can lead to suboptimal results and inaccurate performance estimates. This paper introduces a novel dynamic programming approach to quantum circuit compilation that explicitly addresses the inherent uncertainty associated with qubit measurements and gate operations. The algorithm utilizes probabilistic models to represent the likelihood of measurement outcomes and gate errors, optimizing the circuit design for the *expected* performance, considering the statistical nature of quantum computation. The core contribution lies in shifting the focus from worst-case scenarios to expected outcomes, leading to more realistic and potentially more efficient quantum circuit designs. The methodology provides a framework for incorporating uncertainty directly into the compilation process, a crucial step towards achieving robust and reliable quantum computation.

title: ## Coral Crab Optimization Algorithm (CCOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Coral Crab Optimization Algorithm (CCOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of coral crabs (Stenoplax). Coral crabs, known for their remarkable ability to navigate complex environments and efficiently locate food sources, exhibit a unique strategy involving alternating between exploration and exploitation. CCOA leverages this behavior by simulating coral crab movement within a search space, employing a "crab" representation, a "reef" structure to represent the search space, and a "current" flow mechanism to guide the crabs towards promising regions. The algorithm incorporates adaptive parameters controlling exploration and exploitation, mimicking the crabs' response to environmental changes and food availability. The core of CCOA lies in its dynamic adjustment of crab positions, reef structure, and current flow, aiming to achieve efficient convergence while maintaining a balance between exploring new areas and refining solutions around promising regions. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, operational rules, and provides a conceptual overview, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation.

title: Andean Porcupine Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Andean Porcupine Behavior
abstract: This paper presents the Andean Porcupine Algorithm (APA), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Andean porcupines. The algorithm mimics the porcupines' strategy of strategically selecting and rejecting food sources, leveraging a combination of local search and global exploration. APA utilizes a novel 'spike' mechanism to represent the solution space and a 'foraging' probability to guide the search process. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions. The core of APA lies in its adaptive spike density and rejection probability, dynamically adjusted based on the convergence rate and the quality of the current solution. The proposed algorithm exhibits robust performance and offers a potentially valuable alternative to existing metaheuristic methods, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and multimodal solutions. We explore the algorithm's parameters and their impact on performance, providing insights into its design and applicability. The key mathematical formulations are presented within this document, offering a clear and concise explanation of the APA's operational principles.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Computing Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed computing optimization leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that entanglement can facilitate instantaneous information transfer and coordinated optimization across distributed computing nodes, drastically improving the efficiency of complex computations. The proposed mechanism involves a distributed computing architecture where each node incorporates a quantum processor, utilizing entangled states for communication to enable parallel execution of global optimization algorithms and synchronized results. This approach aims to overcome the limitations imposed by classical communication bottlenecks, capitalizing on the unique properties of quantum mechanics to achieve significant computational gains. We explore the theoretical framework, outlining the key mathematical models and algorithms involved in this entanglement-driven distributed computing system. The system is designed to address challenges inherent in traditional distributed algorithms, offering a potential pathway toward truly scalable and efficient computation. title: Quantum-Inspired Random Walk Algorithms for Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired concepts to enhance the performance of random walk algorithms for optimization problems. Classical random walk algorithms are susceptible to getting trapped in local optima, limiting their efficacy in tackling complex and high-dimensional search spaces. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach that incorporates principles of quantum superposition and tunneling into the random walk process. The algorithm leverages these concepts to enable more extensive exploration of the search space, thereby increasing the probability of converging towards the global optimum. We present a detailed formulation of the algorithm, outlining the key parameters and their influence on the optimization process. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the potential advantages of this quantum-inspired approach compared to traditional random walk methods. The algorithm's ability to escape local minima is evaluated through simulations, showcasing its effectiveness in a variety of benchmark optimization problems. The results highlight the promise of quantum-inspired techniques in improving the robustness and efficiency of random walk algorithms, offering a viable strategy for solving challenging optimization tasks.

title: Evolutionary Algorithm for Compiler Optimization – Graph-Based Representation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to compiler optimization utilizing an evolutionary algorithm. Traditional compiler optimization techniques heavily rely on heuristics, often failing to exploit the full potential of a program's structure for global optimization. Our method addresses this limitation by directly optimizing the control flow graph (CFG) of a program using an evolutionary algorithm. This allows the algorithm to explore a vast search space of possible code transformations, potentially discovering transformations that would be missed by traditional heuristic methods. The core of our approach involves representing the program as a graph and employing an evolutionary algorithm to iteratively refine this graph, aiming to minimize a specified cost function, often representing execution time or code size. We detail the graph-based representation, the evolutionary algorithm design, and the evaluation strategy. The results, though presented without experimental validation due to the nature of this theoretical exploration, demonstrate the potential of this approach for achieving more efficient and novel code transformations.

abstract: 본 연구는 AI가 문법 교육 상황에서 정확하고 체계적인 개념 설명을 제공할 수 있도록, 퀄리아 구 기반의 문법 교육 도메인 지식 그래프를 설계하고 그 작동 가능성을 탐색적으로 확인하는 데 목적이 있다. 이에 고등학교 ‘품사’ 단원을 대상으로 5종의 노드 라벨과 21종의 관계 라벨로 이루어진 속성 그래프를 설계하고 이 구조에 따라 568개의 노드와 1,793개의 관계로 구성된 문법 지식 그래프를 구축하였다.설계된 지식 그래프의 작동 양상을 확인하기 위해 일반 모델, 교과서 원문 참조 모델, 그래프 RAG 적용 모델의 생성 결과를 세 가지 문법 질문에 대해 질적으로 대조하였다. 분석 결과, 그래프 RAG 적용 모델은 ‘서술격 조사’의 분류적 위상, 구성 요소, 기능 등을 함께 제시하였고, ‘ㅂ 불규칙 활용’을 적용 조건, 변화 과정, 결과를 중심으로 서술하였다. 또한 ‘명사’와 ‘어미’를 일정한 기준에 따라 대칭적으로 대조하는 양상을 보였다. 다만 본 연구는 제한된 문항에 대한 탐색적 사례 분석이므로, 퀄리아 기반 구조의 일반적 효과는 후속 연구를 통해 양적으로 검증될 필요가 있다.본 연구는 퀄리아 구조가 국어 문법 교육 지식을 기계 가독형 그래프 구조로 표상하기 위한 설계 원리로 활용될 수 있음을 보이고, 향후 지능형 문법 튜터 구축을 위한 도메인 지식 베이스 설계의 한 가능성을 제시했다는 점에서 의의가 있다.

title: Pemetaan Potensi Panas Bumi Berbasis Pengindraan Jauh di Wilayah Lubuk Sikaping, Kabupaten Pasaman Menggunakan parameter LST, NDVI dan FFD
abstract: Pemetaan indikasi potensi panas bumi dilakukan di wilayah Lubuk Sikaping, Kabupaten Pasaman, menggunakan pendekatan penginderaan jauh berbasis citra satelit untuk mendukung identifikasi awal zona prospek panas bumi di daerah dengan keterbatasan data lapangan. Penelitian ini menggunakan tiga parameter utama, yaitu Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Land Surface Temperature (LST), dan Fault and Fracture Density (FFD), yang masing-masing merepresentasikan kondisi vegetasi, suhu permukaan, serta struktur rekahan dan sesar geologi. Data diperoleh dari citra Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS dan DEM SRTM, yang diolah menggunakan Google Earth Engine (GEE) dan perangkat Sistem Informasi Geografis (SIG). Integrasi ketiga parameter tersebut dilakukan dengan metode Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa nilai NDVI berkisar antara 0,0046 hingga 0,5569, nilai LST antara 15,00 hingga 44,89 °C, dan nilai FFD melebihi 3,2 km/km² pada zona sesar aktif. Zona prospek panas bumi terkonsentrasi di bagian tengah hingga barat laut daerah penelitian, termasuk wilayah yang tidak memiliki manifestasi permukaan. Validasi melalui perbandingan spasial dengan data geologi regional dan manifestasi panas bumi di sekitarnya menunjukkan kesesuaian yang kuat serta mendukung akurasi model. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan berbasis penginderaan jauh memiliki potensi yang signifikan sebagai metode non-invasif untuk identifikasi awal prospek panas bumi dan dapat menjadi referensi yang berharga dalam perencanaan eksplorasi lanjutan di wilayah dengan keterbatasan data pengukuran lapangan.

title: DIALOGOS: A Dialog Chatbot Framework for Eliciting and Mapping Science Misconceptions in Elementary School
abstract: Persistent misconceptions about scientific concepts develop early in elementary education and resist traditional teaching. The diagnostic tools most commonly used to identify them, such as multiple-choice and tiered tests, reveal that an answer is incorrect but not the reasoning behind it. This article presents DIALOGOS (DIAlogic Learning Observatory for the Grasping Of Science), a conceptual framework for a teacher-guided conversational tool that elicits and maps elementary pupils' science misconceptions through natural dialogue. The framework was developed through a theory synthesis of 68 sources identified in Scopus, ERIC, and Google Scholar, comprising 62 peer-reviewed works, two preprints, three books, and one policy report, managed in Zotero and hand-coded in a five-field extraction matrix. Coded claims were integrated through conceptual translation, cross-strand confrontation, and constraint propagation across three areas: conceptual change theory, dialogic teaching, and educational chatbot research. The synthesis yields six design principles and a four-part architecture: a dialogic elicitation engine grounded in Socratic questioning and the elicit–confront–resolve sequence; a mapping module comparing pupils' reasoning against a research-based catalogue and a concept-map overlay; an individual misconception profile; and a class-level observatory for teachers. The framework repositions educational chatbots from answer providers to diagnostic listeners, shifts misconception diagnosis from item-based to conversation-based mapping, and specifies six testable propositions for empirical validation

title: Synthetic Worlds for Temporal Evaluation and Knowledge Updating in LLMs
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) rely on static pretraining corpora, causing their knowledge to become outdated over time. Existing approaches for evaluating knowledge edits either suffer from rapid contamination or rely on counterfactual edits that conflict with rigid existing knowledge. In this work, we propose a synthetic, simulation-driven framework for studying knowledge insertion in LLMs. We introduce {\sc ParallelEvents}, a benchmark of fictional yet realistic future worlds that generates coherent event trajectories for controlled evaluation, avoiding contamination while preserving consistency. Building on this dataset, we develop {\sc Synapse}, a training framework that uses model-generated data to update model parameters via mid-training and instruction tuning. This synthetic pipeline enables scalable knowledge integration without costly human-curated data. Empirically, {\sc Synapse} outperforms existing methods by 14.23\%, demonstrating that simulation-based synthetic training leads to robust and coherent knowledge insertions.

title: Unconditional Certified Randomness without Structure
abstract: We obtain a certified randomness protocol in the quantum random oracle model. The protocol is non-interactive and publicly verifiable with a classical verifier, and is based on Yamakawa and Zhandry's proof of quantumness [JACM'24]. We prove unconditional security of this protocol against adversaries making subexponentially-many adaptive quantum queries to the random oracle. Prior work on certified randomness relative to a random oracle additionally assumed the Aaronson--Ambainis conjecture or proved security only against low query-depth adversaries.

title: Converse and Collision-Based Achievability for Node Localization with Hybrid Distance-Spectral Graph Positional Encodings
abstract: Graph positional encodings are widely used in graph neural networks and graph Transformers, yet it remains unclear when the code itself can identify nodes. We study a hybrid distance-spectral encoding that combines anchor-distance profiles with quantized low-frequency Laplacian-energy coordinates. Treating the encoding as an observation map yields a simplex-refined converse, an exact collision factorization \(κ_H=κ_Dκ_{S|D}\), and the collision information \(I_H=-\logκ_D-\logκ_{S|D}\). On random regular graphs, the criterion is made explicit through a bounded-correlation Gaussian-wave surrogate; for actual Laplacian-energy coordinates, we give the distance-conditioned spectral collision condition sufficient for conditional actual-coordinate achievability. Experiments show that \(I_H/\log n\) calibrates localization success, and PE-only structural task probes on Universal Dependencies trees show that hybrid encodings better recover syntactic-tree geometry than distance-only or spectral-only baselines.

title: Design and Implementation of an Intelligent Accounting Information System Using Machine Learning: Framework and Exploratory Analysis on the PaySim Dataset
abstract: Conventional accounting information systems (AIS) are effective for transaction recording and reporting but have limited capability for fraud risk detection, anomaly identification, predictive analytics, and intelligent decision support. This paper presents the design of an intelligent AIS that integrates machine learning across these functions, supported by an exploratory analysis of the PaySim synthetic financial dataset. Using an applied design science approach, the study specifies a modular architecture comprising data input, storage, preprocessing, feature engineering, supervised fraud detection, anomaly detection, predictive analytics, and decision-support reporting. The dataset contains 6,362,620 transactions, of which 8,213 (approximately 0.13%) are fraudulent. The exploratory analysis reveals severe class imbalance, a concentration of fraud in CASH_OUT and TRANSFER transactions, and very limited coverage by the conventional rule-based fraud flag, which identifies only 16 transactions. These findings demonstrate why fixed rules alone are insufficient and why ML-based analysis is needed within AIS controls. Exploratory prototype evaluation of four supervised models shows that Logistic Regression achieved the highest ROC AUC, while Random Forest achieved the highest F1 score, illustrating the trade-off between ranking performance and minority-class detection. Beyond isolated ML fraud-detection models, this study contributes an implementation-oriented AIS framework that connects fraud detection, anomaly review, predictive analytics, and reporting within a human-in-the-loop accounting control process. Practically, the framework can help accountants prioritize high-risk transactions, manage false-alert workload through appropriate model thresholds, and use ML outputs as evidence for review rather than automatic fraud judgments.

title: TrainTrack Dataset
abstract: The TrainTrack Dataset is a collection of smartphone inertial sensor recordings captured by passengers during real train journeys. It was collected for the paper "On the Same Track: Privacy Leaks in Electric Rail Transport via Magnetic Fields" (CCS '26), which studies how the magnetic field of electric trains leaks through the smartphone magnetometer. What the dataset contains The dataset consists of two parts: traintrack-dataset/ — 487.5 hours of labeled train travel. Recordings from participants who regularly commute by train, covering 217 journeys, 342 trips, and 2,001 station-to-station segments across 246 unique stations. The data is organized hierarchically: a journey is one continuous recording session of a participant's travel, a trip is a single train ride between two changes within a journey, and a segment is one station-to-station leg of a trip. 357 segments were recorded by two or more devices simultaneously aboard the same train, making them usable for colocation studies. Every segment is annotated with the train type and whether the train runs on a 16.7 Hz AC overhead line. The distribution by train type, given as total hours and segments with the 16.7 Hz electric share in parentheses: Long distance — 420.1 h, 862 segments (thereof 16.7 Hz electric: 408.0 h, 840 segments) Regional — 43.5 h, 346 segments (thereof 16.7 Hz electric: 36.4 h, 281 segments) Urban — 19.7 h, 586 segments (thereof 16.7 Hz electric: 3.7 h, 88 segments) Metro — 4.2 h, 201 segments (thereof 16.7 Hz electric: none) Tram — 0.1 h, 6 segments (thereof 16.7 Hz electric: none) Total — 487.5 h, 2,001 segments (thereof 16.7 Hz electric: 448.1 h, 1,209 segments) no-trainride-dataset/ — everyday activity outside of trains. Recordings collected by the same participants while carrying their smartphones through ordinary daily life, serving as negative examples for transport mode detection. These traces are annotated with activity labels from Google's Activity Recognition API and cover roughly 78 hours in total, distributed over stationary periods (~108,000 s), walking (~33,000 s), cycling (~22,000 s), automotive travel (~30,000 s), and unclassified intervals (~90,000 s). Sensors Recordings were made with the Sensor Logger app. Each recording is a set of CSV files, one per sensor, sharing a common journey-relative time base: Magnetometer (calibrated and uncalibrated) Accelerometer (calibrated, uncalibrated, and total acceleration) Gyroscope (calibrated and uncalibrated) Gravity, Orientation, Game Orientation, Geomagnetic Orientation, Compass Barometer Per-recording device metadata (model, platform, app version, sensor list, sample rates) Code and documentation Detailed instructions for downloading, extracting, and working with the dataset, along with the full implementation and experiments from the paper, are available at: https://github.com/mlsec-group/magtrack Citation @inproceedings{czybik2026magtrack, title = {On the Same Track: Privacy Leaks in Electric Rail Transport via Magnetic Fields}, author = {Czybik, Stefan and Hanfeld, Pia and Rieck, Konrad}, booktitle = {Proceedings of the 33rd ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)}, year = {2026} }

title: Quantum Information Entropy Encoding: A Novel Approach Utilizing Quantum Entanglement
abstract: Quantum information entropy, a fundamental concept in quantum physics, represents the uncertainty associated with information. Traditional encoding methods struggle to efficiently represent and transmit this uncertainty, limiting their potential for advanced computation and secure communication. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement as a novel encoding mechanism, proposing a method that leverages the instantaneous correlations inherent in entangled states to create a robust and potentially transformative encoding process. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the design of a quantum entanglement protocol for information encoding, extraction, and compression. The research focuses on the inherent advantages of quantum entanglement over conventional encoding techniques, specifically highlighting its ability to provide enhanced information protection and computational capabilities. We conclude with a discussion of the potential implications and challenges of this approach, emphasizing its promise for revolutionizing information security and quantum computing.

abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum simulation to predict material properties. title: Neuro-Symbolic Program Synthesis via Dynamic Bayesian Networks
abstract: Program synthesis, the automated generation of computer programs, faces significant challenges when dealing with complex, real-world problems. Traditional approaches often rely solely on symbolic methods or neural networks, each with limitations in capturing the full complexity of program logic and data patterns. This paper proposes a novel neuro-symbolic approach that combines the strengths of Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) and neural networks to achieve more effective and adaptable program synthesis. The core idea is to construct a hybrid system where a DBN provides a structured symbolic representation and execution engine, while a neural network learns and refines the probabilistic model of the DBN based on observed program execution outcomes. This iterative process allows the system to dynamically adjust its synthesis strategy, leading to improved program generation accuracy and efficiency. The system's architecture and mechanism are presented, highlighting its ability to integrate symbolic reasoning with neural pattern recognition, ultimately addressing a critical gap in current program synthesis techniques. The system demonstrates the potential to generate complex programs by learning the underlying patterns of successful program executions.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Simulation of Biological Systems
abstract: The simulation of complex biological systems, such as protein folding and gene regulation, presents significant challenges due to the inherent complexity and often intractable nature of these systems. Traditional computational methods struggle to capture the nuanced dynamics of biological processes, limiting our ability to understand and potentially manipulate them. This research proposes an innovative approach – adaptive quantum simulation – that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to create dynamic, self-adjusting simulations of biological systems. This work explores the potential of quantum computation to overcome limitations inherent in classical simulation techniques, offering a fundamentally new pathway for biological system modeling and analysis. This includes a detailed explanation of the algorithm's core mechanisms, potential applications, and preliminary results demonstrating its adaptability. The core claim is that this adaptive quantum simulation method will allow for a level of detail and accuracy previously unattainable through conventional computational methods.

title: Title: Adaptive Metric Learning for Non-Euclidean Data
abstract: The quest for robust and adaptable machine learning models has spurred significant research into learning representations that are less sensitive to variations in the data distribution. Traditional methods often struggle with data drift and require extensive retraining, a costly and time-consuming process. This paper introduces Adaptive Metric Learning (AML), a novel algorithm designed to address these challenges by dynamically adjusting the metric space during the learning process. AML leverages a 'Dynamic Metric Gradient' – a sophisticated AI system – to automatically adapt to data distribution shifts, ensuring improved generalization and robustness. This approach significantly enhances the representational capacity of the model, reducing the need for manual fine-tuning and enabling more reliable performance across diverse datasets. The core mechanism involves an iterative process of gradient estimation, metric adjustment, and validation, all guided by a learned metric landscape. The potential benefits of AML are substantial, offering a promising pathway towards more adaptable and dependable machine learning systems.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network architecture design, drawing inspiration from the intricate structures and functionalities of biological neural networks. The core idea is to leverage bio-inspired algorithms to automatically optimize the architecture and parameters of artificial neural networks. Traditional methods for neural network design often rely on manual tuning or heuristic search, which can be computationally expensive and may not always yield optimal results. title: Quantum-Inspired Feature Selection for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel feature selection method inspired by quantum mechanics, termed Quantum-Inspired Feature Selection (QIFS). Traditional feature selection techniques often struggle to capture complex correlations between features, leading to suboptimal model performance. QIFS leverages the principles of quantum superposition and interference to evaluate feature importance. The core mechanism involves simulating a quantum measurement process, where features are treated as quantum states and their relevance is determined by the interference patterns resulting from interactions. This approach allows for a more nuanced understanding of feature dependencies compared to methods like mutual information or correlation coefficients. The proposed method aims to identify a subset of features that maximizes the overall model performance while minimizing redundancy. The evaluation framework outlined in this paper provides a foundation for future research and development in this promising area. ---

title: # Black Bonneted Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bat Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, "Black Bonneted Bat" (BBB), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Black Bonneted Bat (Hypsignathus monstrosus). The algorithm leverages the bat's echolocation and flight patterns to navigate the search space and converge towards optimal solutions. BBB incorporates elements of pulse-frequency modulation (PFM) for exploration and a modified convergence mechanism mimicking the bat's social interaction. The algorithm's core components include an initial population, a position vector for each individual, a frequency parameter representing exploration intensity, and a loudness parameter controlling the convergence rate. Mathematical formulations describing the update rules for position, frequency, and loudness are detailed. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic methods. The results indicate that BBB offers a robust and adaptable approach for solving complex optimization challenges.

title: Decentralized Learning with Federated Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel decentralized learning algorithm for Bayesian networks, termed Federated Bayesian Networks (FBNs). The core idea is to enable nodes within a network to learn independently and collaboratively, mirroring the principles of federated learning. Each node maintains its own Bayesian network and updates its parameters based on probabilistic information received from its neighbors. This approach avoids the need for centralized data aggregation, addressing key challenges associated with privacy and scalability in traditional Bayesian network learning. The algorithm iteratively refines both the network structure and its parameters, leading to a more accurate and robust global model. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the update rules and convergence properties of the FBN algorithm. The key contribution lies in establishing a framework for distributed Bayesian network learning, particularly well-suited for scenarios with heterogeneous data and limited communication bandwidth. This work lays the foundation for applying FBNs to diverse applications, including healthcare, smart cities, and anomaly detection.

title: Ash-gray Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Ash-gray Mice
abstract: This paper presents Ash-gray Mouse, a new metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's core inspiration stems from the foraging behavior of Ash-gray mice, specifically their tendency to explore densely populated areas before moving to less frequented regions. Ash-gray Mouse leverages a novel exploration-exploitation strategy based on a dynamic density map and a weighted random movement system. The algorithm employs a population of potential solutions, represented as vectors, and iteratively updates these solutions using a combination of local search and global search operators. The density map dynamically reflects the "visitedness" of each solution space, encouraging exploration in under-explored areas. A weighted random movement mechanism, influenced by the density map and solution quality, guides the search process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Ash-gray Mouse through simulations on a variety of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, the Sphere function, and the Powell test functions. The results indicate that Ash-gray Mouse achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and the Particle Swarm Optimization. The algorithm's adaptability and efficient exploration-exploitation balance make it a promising approach for a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: Quantum-Inspired Simulation of Biological Neuronal Networks
abstract: Biological neuronal networks represent a fundamental component of complex systems, including the brain. Simulating these networks accurately and efficiently is a significant challenge, largely due to the intricate, non-linear interactions between neurons. Traditional simulation methods, often relying on numerical integration techniques like the Hodgkin-Huxley model, are computationally intensive, particularly when scaling to large networks. This paper proposes a novel approach to neuronal network simulation inspired by quantum mechanics, specifically leveraging concepts of superposition and entanglement. We introduce a framework that utilizes quantum-inspired algorithms to represent and evolve neuronal states, aiming to dramatically reduce computational overhead. The core idea involves mapping neuronal dynamics onto a quantum system, where neurons are represented by qubits, and synaptic connections are modeled as quantum gates. The simulation process then utilizes quantum algorithms to evolve the system, effectively capturing the parallel and interconnected nature of neuronal networks. We present a mathematical formulation of the simulation process, focusing on the evolution equation for neuronal states. We explore key concepts like wave function collapse and measurement in the context of neuronal network simulation, offering a potential pathway for more realistic and efficient modeling of biological neural systems. The ultimate goal is to provide a computationally tractable method for simulating large-scale neuronal networks, leading to improved understanding of brain function and potentially facilitating the development of advanced neurotechnologies. The presented framework offers a distinct alternative to conventional methods, promising significant advantages in terms of speed and scalability.

title: ## The Black Crown Crane Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCIMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Black Crown Crane Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCIMA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's design is directly inspired by the foraging behavior of Black Crown Cranes, specifically their strategic exploration and exploitation of resources in a dynamic environment. BCIMA leverages a multi-layered, hierarchical approach, mirroring the crane's social structure and hunting strategies. It incorporates a 'territory' concept, similar to a crane's established feeding ground, and a 'migration' mechanism to encourage diversification and escape local optima. The algorithm utilizes a novel 'assessment' function based on resource availability and competitive pressure, dynamically adjusting the search process. The core of BCIMA lies in its adaptive weight system, which continuously modifies the influence of exploration and exploitation based on the observed performance landscape. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, mathematical formulation, and design principles, establishing a foundation for future research and applications.

title: Angolan Brush-furred Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by its Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Brush-furred Rat Algorithm" (BFRA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Angolan brush-furred rat. These rats are renowned for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in complex, unpredictable environments. The algorithm leverages key aspects of their movement patterns, including exploration, exploitation, and obstacle avoidance, to develop a robust optimization approach. BFRA employs a population-based search strategy with a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance. The algorithm's core mechanics involve a 'pheromone trail' system, mirroring the rat's ability to learn and remember rewarding locations, and a simulated 'obstacle avoidance' mechanism based on the rat's spatial awareness. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's design, its underlying principles, and its performance through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples. The primary goal is to demonstrate the effectiveness of BFRA in solving various optimization problems, showcasing its potential as a valuable addition to the metaheuristic landscape. Specifically, we demonstrate BFRA's efficacy on the Rastrigin and Sphere functions, comparing its performance to established algorithms like the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The results indicate that BFRA consistently achieves competitive, and in some cases superior, solutions with reduced computational complexity.

title: Angola Colobus-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Colobus," inspired by the foraging behavior of Angola colobus monkeys. These monkeys exhibit a complex and adaptive strategy for locating food resources, characterized by exploration, exploitation, and a dynamic adjustment of search parameters based on environmental feedback. The Colobus algorithm leverages these principles to develop a new optimization technique. The algorithm incorporates a novel adaptive parameter control mechanism, utilizing a 'resource density' concept mirroring the colobus's assessment of food availability. This density is dynamically adjusted through a weighted sum of past successful moves and random exploration. The algorithm employs a population-based approach with a unique 'social learning' component, where individuals share information about promising regions of the search space, promoting convergence while maintaining exploration capabilities. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic methods like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that Colobus is a promising approach for tackling complex optimization challenges, particularly those exhibiting non-convexity and multi-modality.

title: Quantum Bayesian Model Optimization Algorithm based on Gaussian Distribution, QBOMA
abstract: Quantum Bayesian Model Optimization (QBOMA) is a novel optimization algorithm designed to enhance the performance of quantum probability models. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with parameter diffusion and deviation from target states, particularly in complex quantum systems. This paper introduces QBOMA, a framework that leverages the properties of the Gaussian distribution to achieve robust parameter control and improve the overall optimization process. The core mechanism of QBOMA centers around the use of Gaussian distributions as the probability distribution for quantum model parameters, enabling a structured approach to parameter adjustment that minimizes unwanted fluctuations and promotes convergence towards optimal states. This approach offers a significant improvement in stability and efficiency compared to existing optimization techniques, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional quantum spaces.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive aggregation strategy for quantum graphs based on nonlinear quantum graphs. The core mechanism involves establishing a dynamic self-organizing structure within the quantum graph, allowing for adaptive weighting of graph elements based on input data. This approach addresses the limitations of static aggregation techniques and offers a promising path toward improved quantum computation. The paper details the design of the algorithm, its implementation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in a specific quantum algorithm.

title: ##基于多模态数据融合的因果推理算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for causal inference leveraging the fusion of multiple modalities. The core challenge in causal inference lies in the inherent limitations of relying solely on a single data source. Traditional causal inference methods often struggle when dealing with heterogeneous data, leading to inaccurate or incomplete causal relationships. This research addresses this challenge by integrating deep learning models for feature extraction from diverse modalities and subsequently employing a causal inference algorithm, specifically a structural causal model (SCM), on the fused data. The proposed approach overcomes the modality constraints of conventional causal inference techniques, offering a more robust and comprehensive understanding of causal relationships within complex systems. The algorithm is designed to handle data from various sources, such as text, images, and numerical data, ultimately enhancing the accuracy and reliability of causal reasoning. This work contributes to advancements in areas requiring nuanced causal understanding, including healthcare diagnostics, autonomous systems, and social science research. ---

title: Title: Universal Quantum Time Synchronization via Entangled Oscillators
abstract: Quantum time measurement is a fundamental challenge in quantum information theory, posing a significant hurdle in the development of quantum technologies. Traditional time synchronization methods often rely on classical systems and are susceptible to errors and limitations. This paper explores a novel approach to universal quantum time synchronization leveraging the principles of entangled oscillators. We propose a method utilizing entangled oscillators to generate a correlated temporal signature, enabling the establishment of a universal time reference through measurement and comparison. The core mechanism centers around creating and analyzing entanglement between oscillators, which inherently correlates temporal events across different quantum systems. This research contributes to a foundational understanding of time synchronization within the quantum realm, potentially opening avenues for more robust and reliable quantum communication and computation. The proposed method offers a pathway toward achieving a truly universal time reference, addressing limitations inherent in existing synchronization techniques.

title: Title: Adaptive Error Correction in Quantum Error Correction Networks
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical enabling technology for quantum computation, offering the potential for fault-tolerant quantum computers. However, the inherent fragility of quantum states necessitates sophisticated error correction schemes. Static error correction protocols, while conceptually simple, struggle to maintain optimal performance in the presence of fluctuating error rates. This paper introduces an adaptive error correction scheme leveraging Bayesian principles and a dynamic parameter adjustment algorithm to enhance the fidelity of quantum computations. The core mechanism centers on a 'Bayesian Error Correction' algorithm that continuously monitors error rates and dynamically adjusts correction parameters to maximize quantum fidelity. We analyze the potential advantages of this approach, focusing on improved robustness and adaptability to evolving error profiles within quantum error correction networks. The proposed scheme is presented with detailed mathematical formulations and illustrative examples, demonstrating its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and simulation.

abstract: This paper introduces the Altai Pika Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (APIMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm designed to leverage the adaptive and resilient behaviors observed in the Altai pika (Ochotona altai). The algorithm incorporates elements of the pika's foraging strategy, including risk assessment, resource prioritization, and opportunistic movement, into a new iterative search process. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The key contributions of this work include the novel application of pika-inspired heuristics and a detailed analysis of the algorithm's parameters and their impact on performance. The overall aim is to propose a robust and efficient metaheuristic approach capable of tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: 基于量子计算的密码学算法优化
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of cryptographic algorithms leveraging the potential of quantum computing. The core claim is that quantum computing's computational power can be harnessed to enhance the efficiency and security of existing cryptographic algorithms. The primary mechanism involves utilizing quantum simulators to model and analyze quantum cryptography algorithms, aiming to identify more efficient and secure key generation and decryption protocols. This work addresses the looming threat posed by quantum computers to current cryptographic standards, specifically focusing on improving security through algorithmic refinement. The research explores potential improvements in algorithms like RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) considering quantum attacks, and investigates novel approaches to quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols. This paper contributes to the ongoing discourse on post-quantum cryptography by offering a theoretical framework for optimization based on quantum simulation and analysis. The exploration includes examining the impact of quantum algorithms on the security parameters of established cryptographic systems and proposing strategies for mitigating quantum threats. Finally, this work advocates for a proactive approach to cryptographic algorithm development, integrating quantum considerations from the outset.

title: Graph Embeddings with Contrastive Learning for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Knowledge graph completion (KGC) is a crucial task in leveraging the wealth of information stored in knowledge graphs. Traditional graph embedding methods often struggle to capture the complex relationships and structural nuances within these graphs, leading to suboptimal performance in tasks such as link prediction. This paper proposes a novel approach to KGC utilizing contrastive learning. We introduce a model that learns entity embeddings by explicitly contrasting similar and dissimilar entities within the knowledge graph. This is achieved through a carefully designed contrastive loss function that encourages embeddings of related entities to be close together while pushing embeddings of unrelated entities apart. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, showing significant improvements compared to established graph embedding techniques. The core claim is that contrastive learning provides a powerful mechanism for enhancing the quality of graph embeddings. The primary mechanism involves learning to differentiate between similar and dissimilar entities using a contrastive loss. This new approach offers a promising direction for advancing KGC research.

title: The Pecking Parrot Metaheuristic: A Novel Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Woodpecker Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Pecking Parrot Metaheuristic (PPMH), a novel optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of woodpeckers. PPMH leverages the woodpecker's instinctive pecking strategy, characterized by alternating between exploratory and exploitative phases, to navigate search spaces effectively. The algorithm incorporates a 'pecking radius' parameter to define the search area, a 'peck frequency' to control the balance between exploration and exploitation, and a 'memory' mechanism mimicking the woodpecker's retention of preferred feeding locations. PPMH's core mechanism involves iteratively selecting points within a defined radius, evaluating their fitness, and adjusting the search area based on the best fitness found. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, PPMH's design emphasizes adaptability and resilience in complex, multi-dimensional search landscapes, aiming for rapid convergence while avoiding premature convergence. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, operational rules, and conceptual basis, highlighting its potential advantages over existing methods.

title: ## Abyssal Horror: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Deep-Sea Gulper Shark
abstract: This paper introduces Abyssal Horror, a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the hunting strategies and adaptive behaviors of the deep-sea gulper shark ( *Centrophorus granulosus*). Gulper sharks exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating and capturing prey in the extreme, resource-scarce environment of the abyssal zone. Abyssal Horror leverages these characteristics – particularly ambush predation, opportunistic feeding, and dynamic territory adjustment – to create a robust and adaptable optimization process. The algorithm employs a novel 'Pressure Gradient' mechanism to simulate the shark's sensory perception and prey attraction, combined with a 'Territorial Shift' strategy mirroring the shark's adaptation to fluctuating resource availability. We present a mathematical formulation of the algorithm, detailing its key components and operational rules. This paper focuses on the theoretical design and conceptual framework of Abyssal Horror, laying the groundwork for future empirical validation and application to diverse optimization problems.

evidence.title: Adaptive Topology Parameter Adjustment Algorithm
evidence.abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive topology parameter adjustment algorithm designed to optimize the distribution of data within machine learning models. Traditional approaches rely on manual parameter tuning, while this algorithm dynamically adjusts topology parameters, enabling automated optimization. The core mechanism centers around a self-adaptive adjustment process, which iteratively refines the model's representation and improves its predictive capabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through a series of experiments involving a dataset frequently used in classification tasks. The results highlight the algorithm's ability to significantly improve model performance compared to baseline methods.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Wavefunction Collapse for Signal Processing
abstract: Quantum-enhanced wavefunction collapse offers a potentially transformative approach to signal processing, addressing limitations in traditional computational methods. This paper explores the concept of utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition to accelerate the collapse of a wavefunction, resulting in enhanced detection and filtering capabilities. We delve into a proposed quantum algorithm that strategically manipulates quantum states to expedite this crucial step in the signal processing pipeline. The core mechanism involves a carefully designed quantum circuit that exploits the inherent properties of entanglement and superposition to drastically reduce the time required for wavefunction evaluation. This research investigates the theoretical underpinnings, potential advantages, and challenges associated with this quantum-driven paradigm shift. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate a significant improvement in detection and filtering accuracy compared to classical algorithms.

title: ## The Grey Jay Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GJMOA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Grey Jay Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GJMOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Grey Jays ( *Perisoreus canadensis* ). Grey Jays are known for their unique and efficient foraging strategies, particularly their ability to rapidly adapt to changing environmental conditions and exploit sparse food resources. GJMOA leverages these characteristics through a combination of adaptive population management, a novel exploration-exploitation balance mechanism based on perceived food density, and a dynamic Lévy flight-inspired movement strategy. The algorithm's core components – the Adaptive Population Control (APC) mechanism, the Food Density-Based Exploration-Exploitation (FDEE) mechanism, and the Lévy Flight Movement (LFM) strategy – are detailed. While this paper focuses on the theoretical framework and algorithm design, it lays the groundwork for potential future experimental validation and comparison with established metaheuristic techniques.

title: Title: Fractal Dimension-Based Parameter Tuning for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of fractal dimension as a parameter tuning method for machine learning models. Traditional parameter optimization methods often rely on grid search or gradient descent, which can be computationally expensive and may not always converge to optimal solutions. We propose a novel approach where the model's performance is continuously monitored using fractal dimension, allowing for adaptive adjustments to parameters to maximize predictive accuracy. The core mechanism involves establishing a relationship between the fractal dimension and model performance, iteratively refining parameter values based on this relationship. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this method in several benchmark datasets, showcasing potential improvements in model generalization and performance compared to existing techniques. The research explores the benefits of this approach in scenarios where model complexity is high, and parameter optimization is crucial for achieving desired performance.

title: MITIGASI BIAS LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL MELALUI HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP PADA AUTOMATED ESSAY SCORING BERBASIS ESAI IELTS-LIKE
abstract: This study evaluates the reliability, algorithmic bias, and feasibility of implementing Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) in Large Language Model (LLM)-based Automated Essay Scoring (AES). Two architectures were compared: the Mixture-of-Experts architecture represented by GPT OSS 120B and the Dense architecture represented by Qwen3-32B, using a multiple-run scoring approach on 150 IELTS-like essays written by 50 respondents. Each essay was evaluated five times across four criteria: Grammar, Lexical Resource, Coherence, and Task Achievement. The evaluation employed the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC), Coefficient of Variation (CV), score range, paired t-test, and confidence-based routing simulation.The results show that GPT OSS 120B achieved higher reliability, with an ICC of 0.94, an average range of 2.40 points, and a CV of 4.69%, while Qwen3-32B obtained an ICC of 0.84, an average range of 5.56 points, and a CV of 9.17%. However, GPT OSS 120B experienced a parsing failure rate of 25.4%, whereas Qwen3-32B demonstrated full format compliance. Comparative analysis also showed that GPT OSS 120B tended to score more strictly, while Qwen3-32B was more lenient. In the Data Report task without visual input, both models exhibited conservatism bias due to contextual limitations. The HITL simulation showed that GPT OSS 120B could automatically approve 55.4% of essays, compared with only 7.8% for Qwen3-32B. These findings highlight the importance of HITL in maintaining the reliability, fairness, and integrity of academic assessment.
