title: A Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Framework for Intrusion Detection in Healthcare IoT Environments
abstract: Healthcare Internet of Things (HIoT) deployments generate sensitive patient telemetry data on resource-constrained edge devices, which are prime targets for network intrusions. Centralizing raw telemetry for training intrusion detection system (IDS) models violates patient privacy and contravenes data-protection regulations such as HIPAA and GDPR. This paper proposes PPFL-IDS, a Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning framework for intrusion detection in HIoT environments. PPFL-IDS combines federated model aggregation with differential privacy noise injection and secure aggregation protocols to train a lightweight gradient-boosted ensemble IDS without exposing local device data. A heterogeneity-aware client selection mechanism addresses the challenge of non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data inherent in multi-site HIoT deployments. Evaluated on the UNSW-NB15 and a synthetic HIoT dataset spanning five attack categories, PPFL-IDS achieves a weighted F1-score of 0.938 and a mean detection latency of 20.3 ms, outperforming FedAvg, FedProx, and SCAFFOLD baselines while satisfying an ε-differential privacy budget of 1.2. Results demonstrate that strong privacy guarantees and high detection accuracy can be achieved simultaneously in federated HIoT security architectures.

title: Investigation of Optimal Tilt Angle for Solar PV Panels in Lhasa
abstract: Solar energy is a rapidly growing renewable energy resource in the Tibetan Plateau, where high altitude and clear skies provide exceptional solar irradiance. The tilt angle of photovoltaic (PV) panels significantly affects the amount of solar radiation received and consequently the energy output of PV systems. This study investigates the optimal tilt angle for solar PV panels in Lhasa, Tibet (29.65°N, 91.13°E, 3,656 m elevation) during winter. Solar irradiance measurements were collected at ten different tilt angles ranging from 36° to 45° at hourly intervals from 9:00 to 17:00 over three consecutive clear-sky days in January 2025. Statistical analysis revealed that the 44° tilt angle yielded the highest average irradiance of 815.2 W/m² and the maximum daily total irradiation of 7.07 kWh/m²/day. The performance difference across the 36°–45° range was relatively modest (3.3%), with angles between 41° and 45° all exceeding 800 W/m² average irradiance. Afternoon irradiance was consistently higher than morning irradiance across all tilt angles, with peak values occurring between 13:00 and 14:00. These findings provide practical guidance for the design and installation of solar PV systems in the Lhasa region and contribute to the optimization of solar energy utilization in high-altitude plateau environments.

title: Autonomous Attack-Defence Co-Evolution: Measuring the Security Half-Life of AI Controls
abstract: The first empirical measurement of defensive control durability under adaptive adversarial pressure. SPECTER BATTLE LAB v1.0.0 pits WARLORD PRIME (offensive orchestrator, NIGHTFALL, 281 tools, 191 attack layers) against AI Shield FORTRESS v2.0.0 (defensive orchestrator, 216 modules, 17 verticals) in 20 autonomous co-evolution cycles. Both sides adapt. No human in the loop. All results cryptographically signed. Security Half-Life T½ = 13 cycles. Defence peaks at AADR 73.92 (RESILIENT) at cycle 1. DDR degrades at 5% per cycle. Containment collapses at cycle 7. DEGRADED threshold crossed at cycle 14. Equilibrium at AADR 47.95 from cycle 19 — attacker advantage established. WARLORD achieves dominance through tool rotation, learning which FORTRESS modules detect which tools across cycles. FORTRESS deploys 8 real AI Shield modules per cycle (M1, M2, M9, M10, M11, M15, M19, M50). M999 SENTINEL SWARM adapt_rate improves from 0.05 to 0.35 but cannot overcome compounding 5% per-cycle effectiveness loss. These are not simulated results. FORTRESS v2.0.0 executed real defence cycles. 20 BTL-{hex12} signed evidence reports. 1,350 tests. SPECTER AUDIT 6/6. The attacker adapts. The defender adapts. We measure the Security Half-Life.

title: 基于动态自律的矩阵分解的量子计算算法
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for unprecedented computational power, but current algorithms often struggle with scalability and stability. This paper introduces a novel matrix decomposition algorithm, termed "Dynamic Self-Regulation Matrix Decomposition" (DSMRD), designed to address these challenges. DSMRD leverages self-adaptive parameters to optimize the matrix decomposition process, resulting in improved efficiency and stability compared to existing methods. We present a detailed mathematical formulation of the algorithm, including the key parameters and optimization process. The paper explores the theoretical foundations and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of DSMRD in various quantum algorithms. The core mechanism hinges on a dynamically adjusting set of parameters that governs the matrix decomposition, leading to a more robust and adaptable approach. We also discuss potential future research directions, including the exploration of different parameterization strategies and the application of DSMRD to more complex quantum systems.

title: Adaptive Differential Privacy via Kernel-Based Perturbation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to differential privacy, termed Adaptive Differential Privacy via Kernel-Based Perturbation. The core idea is to move beyond the limitations of fixed, uniform noise addition by dynamically adjusting the level of perturbation based on a kernel density estimation of the sensitive data. Specifically, we leverage kernel density estimation (KDE) to model the local distribution of data points, and then scale the added noise proportionally to the KDE's estimate of local density. This adaptive strategy provides a tighter privacy-utility trade-off, offering stronger differential privacy guarantees while minimizing the impact on data utility. The proposed method demonstrates improved performance compared to traditional methods, particularly in scenarios with heterogeneous data distributions. The key contribution lies in the dynamic adjustment of perturbation, driven by the data itself, rather than a static, global parameter. The theoretical analysis provides a formal framework for understanding and quantifying the privacy-utility trade-offs inherent in this approach.

title: Topology-Guided Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces Topology-Guided Evolutionary Algorithms (TGEA), a novel approach to optimization that leverages topology to constrain the search space of evolutionary algorithms, resulting in more robust and adaptable solutions. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often struggle with complex, high-dimensional spaces, leading to premature convergence and suboptimal solutions. TGEA effectively mitigates this problem by incorporating topology as a crucial component of the evolutionary process. We demonstrate the efficacy of TGEA through a series of experiments on a diverse range of optimization problems, consistently achieving superior performance compared to conventional evolutionary algorithms and other topology-based methods. The core mechanism focuses on introducing and utilizing graph-based topology to guide the search, fostering a more structured exploration of the solution space.

title: 基于弦性的量子态的计算效率优化
abstract: Quantum computing, a revolutionary paradigm of computation, offers immense potential for scientific discovery and technological advancement. However, current quantum computing architectures face significant challenges in terms of computational complexity, particularly in the design and implementation of quantum algorithms. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging the principles of string theory to optimize quantum computation, aiming to significantly improve its computational efficiency. We propose a method that structurally modifies the quantum state to enhance the probability of correct outcomes, ultimately reducing the computational resources required for complex calculations. This work details the theoretical framework underpinning the optimization, including the mathematical formulation of the string-based approach and its potential impact on specific quantum algorithms. Our analysis demonstrates that this method offers a substantial improvement over existing optimization techniques, particularly in scenarios involving high-dimensional quantum states. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the potential impact of this technique on the broader field of quantum computing.

title: Hyper-Dimensionality Analysis for Quantum Simulation
abstract: This paper investigates the challenges and opportunities presented by hyper-dimensional spaces in quantum simulation. Quantum systems often exist in high-dimensional configurations, demanding sophisticated simulation techniques. We propose a novel technique, "Dimensionality-Aware Entanglement Mapping," designed to analyze and predict the behavior of these systems, offering insights into the limitations of current simulation methods. The core mechanism relies on a dynamically adjusted entanglement mapping that explores the intricate interplay between entanglement and dimensionality. This approach addresses a critical challenge in quantum simulation by explicitly incorporating the dimensionality of the system being simulated. The resulting analysis provides a framework for understanding and ultimately improving the accuracy and efficiency of quantum simulations.

title: Quantum Topology Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of mathematics, offers a unique approach to manipulating and controlling quantum systems. This paper introduces an Adaptive Algorithm based on Quantum Topology, designed to automatically optimize quantum system parameters through the exploitation of quantum topology's inherent structural constraints. The algorithm leverages the concept of "topology" – a mathematical structure that preserves distances and shapes – to iteratively refine quantum states, leading to more precise control and enhanced system performance. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, highlighting its potential to revolutionize quantum control methodologies.

title: ##基于过程神经网络的程序合成
abstract: This paper explores the potential of process neural networks (PNNs) for program synthesis – the automated generation of executable code from high-level specifications. The core idea is to leverage PNNs' ability to learn complex dynamics directly from observed system behavior, thereby eliminating the need for explicit, hand-crafted programming rules. We present a framework utilizing a PNN to translate system behavior descriptions into corresponding program code. The system learns the underlying dynamics and generates code that accurately replicates the desired system behavior. This approach represents a novel direction in program synthesis, capitalizing on the representational power of neural networks and offering a potentially more intuitive and efficient method for automating code creation. The paper details the architecture of the PNN, the training methodology, and demonstrates the capability of the system to synthesize simple programs based on dynamic system specifications. Further research will focus on scaling this approach to more complex systems and incorporating more sophisticated specification methods.

title: Quantum Key Distribution Based Privacy Computation Protocol
abstract: This paper presents a novel privacy computation protocol leveraging Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) for enhanced data privacy. The core idea is to utilize the principles of QKD to generate a shared secret key, which is then employed to perform computations on encrypted data, ensuring the confidentiality of the results. This approach addresses the fundamental challenge of traditional computation, where data is vulnerable to interception and manipulation during processing. The protocol details the key management process, the encryption/decryption scheme based on QKD, and the computation steps undertaken using the shared key. The proposed system offers a significant advancement in privacy-preserving computation, particularly in scenarios where data sensitivity is paramount. The design focuses on minimizing the computational overhead associated with QKD while maximizing the level of privacy protection. This work lays the groundwork for future research and development in privacy-preserving quantum computing and communication.

abstract: This paper introduces Algorithmic Multiverse Sampling (AMS), a novel self-improving algorithm designed to generate statistically diverse and complex mathematical structures. Traditional methods often suffer from inherent bias, limiting the breadth of potential solutions. AMS overcomes this limitation by leveraging a latent space representation of mathematical concepts, enabling iterative feedback loops that dynamically evolve the underlying structure, producing a vastly expanded and diverse set of mathematical possibilities.

title: 基于自适应混沌的自适应机器学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm, termed "Adaptive Chaos-Driven Machine Learning" (ACDM), that leverages the principles of chaos theory to dynamically adjust model parameters, enhancing model generalization. Traditional machine learning algorithms often rely on static parameters, limiting their adaptability to data patterns. ACDM employs a self-adaptive approach by incorporating a chaotic system, allowing the model to evolve in response to input data, resulting in improved performance across diverse datasets. We present a detailed methodology involving the creation of a chaotic system, parameter adjustment based on its behavior, and validation of the resulting model through extensive testing. The core mechanism centers around the continuous monitoring and manipulation of the system's dynamics to optimize model fit.

title: Title: Computational Geometry of Cognitive Processes
abstract: Cognitive processes represent a complex landscape of emergent phenomena, often difficult to model through traditional computational approaches. This paper explores the potential of computational geometry to simulate these processes by leveraging fractal geometry and network theory. We propose a novel model that visualizes the hierarchical organization of cognitive functions, simulating information flow and processing through dynamically generated geometric structures. The core claim is that by applying geometric algorithms, we can effectively model the emergence of attention, memory, and decision-making – key cognitive phenomena – within a computational framework. This work aims to provide a new perspective on the representation and analysis of cognitive systems, moving beyond purely symbolic models towards a geometric, dynamic representation. The paper details the core mechanism, utilizing fractal geometry to represent hierarchical structures and network theory to model interactions within cognitive networks.

abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly developing field, offers a novel approach to validating quantum computing models and optimizing their performance. title: ## The Bini Free-Tailed Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BFBIMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Bini Free-Tailed Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BFBIMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bini free-tailed bat ( *Carollia perforata*). Bini bats are known for their sophisticated echolocation and efficient foraging strategies within complex environments. BFBIMA leverages these principles, specifically the bat's use of frequency-modulated calls and their ability to adapt their search patterns based on received echoes, to construct a new optimization framework. The algorithm utilizes a dynamic frequency modulation scheme to represent the decision space, coupled with an adaptive echo response mechanism to guide the search towards promising regions. We present a detailed explanation of the algorithm's core components, including the frequency modulation function, the echo response model, and the population update strategy. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's potential for convergence and efficiency in solving a range of optimization problems. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations and comparisons against established metaheuristic algorithms, showcasing its effectiveness in tackling challenging optimization tasks. The key contributions of this work are the innovative application of bat echolocation principles to metaheuristic design and the provision of a robust and adaptable optimization algorithm.

title: Based on Information Entropy: A Program Adaptive Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive optimization algorithm that leverages the concept of information entropy to dynamically adjust optimization parameters during program execution. Traditional optimization algorithms often rely on fixed parameters, which may not be optimal for all problems. This algorithm addresses this limitation by utilizing the variability in information entropy as a feedback signal, providing a dynamic mechanism for parameter adjustment. Specifically, the algorithm calculates the information entropy of the program's execution process in real-time and uses this value to modify parameters such as the learning rate and exploration probability. The core claim of this work is that utilizing the change in program execution information entropy as a feedback signal, can dynamically adjust program optimization algorithm parameters, achieve self-adaptive optimization. The core mechanism is the real-time calculation of the information entropy of the program execution process, and using it as the basis for algorithm parameter adjustment, such as adjusting the learning rate and exploration probability. This approach offers a potentially more efficient and robust optimization strategy compared to traditional methods. ---

title: Bayesian Deep Learning with Causal Discovery for Feature Selection
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of current feature selection techniques within deep learning, which frequently rely on empirical correlations rather than a robust causal understanding. We propose a novel framework that integrates Bayesian deep learning with causal discovery algorithms to identify features that possess a genuine causal relationship with the target variable. The core idea is to leverage the probabilistic reasoning inherent in Bayesian deep learning alongside the ability of causal discovery methods to uncover underlying causal structures. This approach aims to move beyond spurious correlations and build more accurate, interpretable, and robust deep learning models. We outline the methodology, detailing the incorporation of causal discovery into the Bayesian deep learning process, and discuss potential applications and future research directions. The framework offers a significant advancement in feature selection, providing a theoretically grounded approach that can substantially improve deep learning model performance.

title: ## The Whale Shark Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (WISAS)
abstract: This paper introduces the Whale Shark Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (WISAS), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and social dynamics of whale sharks. WISAS leverages the whale shark's unique ability to maintain a stable group while dynamically adjusting its search strategy based on environmental factors—specifically, the relative position and density of other sharks. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a "herd" of potential solutions and a "leader" shark to guide the search. Adaptive parameters are adjusted based on the shark's relative position within the group, mimicking the whale shark's avoidance of congested areas and attraction to resource-rich zones. The core innovation lies in the dynamically adjusted exploration and exploitation balance within the search process, promoting efficient convergence while maintaining robustness. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and underlying principles, demonstrating its potential for solving complex optimization problems.

title: ## The Coral Current Optimization Algorithm (CCOA): Inspired by the Behavior of Dragonfish
abstract: This paper introduces the Coral Current Optimization Algorithm (CCOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the unique hunting behavior of dragonfish (Melanocetus johnsonii). Dragonfish utilize a "coral current" strategy – a coordinated, pulsed stream of water generated by rapid, rhythmic movements of their pectoral fins – to efficiently locate and capture prey in the dark depths of the ocean. CCOA leverages this strategy by representing solutions as "currents" within a search space. The algorithm iteratively adjusts the velocity and direction of these currents, mimicking the dragonfish's synchronized movement and pulsed emission. Key components include a current weighting mechanism, a directional adjustment strategy based on prey density estimation, and a dynamic pulse rate adjustment to enhance convergence. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, detailing its core principles and operational mechanics. While experimental validation is deferred to future work, this paper establishes a robust foundation for CCOA and its potential applications in diverse optimization problems.

title: ## Aquitanian Mole: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Microtus aquaticus*
abstract: This paper introduces Aquitanian Mole, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of the Aquitanian mole (*Microtus aquaticus*), a small rodent endemic to southwestern France. Moles are renowned for their efficient and adaptive underground navigation and food-seeking behavior. Aquitanian Mole leverages key aspects of this behavior – specifically, the use of scent trails, exploratory movements, and risk-averse decision-making – to create a robust and effective optimization algorithm. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a virtual 'mole' to explore the search space. Movement is governed by a stochastic process influenced by 'scent' (represented by gradient information), while the algorithm incorporates a risk aversion parameter to balance exploration and exploitation. We present the algorithm's theoretical underpinnings, its core components, and demonstrate its efficacy through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that Aquitanian Mole exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods, particularly in challenging landscapes with discontinuities and local optima. Future research directions include exploring variations in the scent trail dynamics and integrating the algorithm with machine learning techniques.

title: Causal Discovery from Streaming Data with Granger Causality and Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of causal discovery in dynamic environments where data arrives continuously—a scenario often referred to as streaming data. Traditional causal discovery algorithms typically rely on static datasets, rendering them unsuitable for this context. This work proposes a novel algorithm that integrates Granger causality tests with Bayesian networks to perform causal inference in real-time from streaming data. The algorithm leverages Granger causality to identify potential temporal dependencies between variables, followed by Bayesian network construction to refine the inferred causal relationships. The core claim is that dynamic causal inference is possible and can be effectively performed by this method. The core mechanism is the combination of Granger causality and Bayesian networks. This approach provides a pathway for understanding causal relationships in evolving datasets, offering significant improvements over existing methods. The presented algorithm's capability to handle dynamic causal inference in streaming data scenarios makes it a valuable tool for various applications, including anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, and real-time decision-making.

abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Blackfish Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BMHOA), inspired by the hunting strategies of Blackfish ( *Melanocetus johnsonii*). title: Quantum Degradation Modeling and Adaptive Optimization for Error Correction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum error correction (QEC) that leverages quantum degradation modeling and adaptive optimization. Traditional QEC methods often employ fixed error correction codes, which may not be optimal for specific quantum hardware due to varying noise characteristics. Our approach addresses this limitation by dynamically adjusting the parameters of the QEC code based on a model of the degradation introduced by the quantum hardware. We establish a quantum degradation model, analyze the noise distribution using machine learning algorithms, and then optimize the parameters of the error correction code – such as code length and encoding rate – to achieve maximum quantum information transmission efficiency. The core contribution lies in the iterative feedback loop between the degradation model, the noise analysis, and the adaptive parameter adjustment, leading to a significantly improved QEC performance compared to static code implementations. This work offers a pathway towards more robust and efficient quantum communication and computation.

title: Probabilistic Robotics with Continuous-Time Bayesian Filtering
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of traditional discrete-time Bayesian filtering in probabilistic robotics, particularly when dealing with systems exhibiting continuous-time dynamics. The core argument presented here is that relying solely on discrete-time filtering introduces inaccuracies due to the inherent continuous evolution of robot states. This work proposes and develops a novel probabilistic robotics model utilizing continuous-time Bayesian filtering, offering a more faithful representation of robot dynamics. The model employs the following key elements: a continuous-state space description, a continuous-time process noise model, and a continuous-time observation model. The theoretical framework is built upon the principles of stochastic calculus and Kalman filtering theory, adapted for continuous-time systems. The benefits of this approach are demonstrated through a detailed analysis, highlighting improved accuracy and realism in robotic system performance within complex, real-world environments. The primary contribution lies in providing a robust and efficient method for state estimation in robotics where continuous dynamics are dominant, ultimately leading to better control and decision-making for robotic agents.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Hierarchical Attention Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel architecture for neuro-symbolic reasoning, termed the Hierarchical Attention Network (HAN). The core challenge in integrating neural networks and symbolic reasoning lies in effectively transferring knowledge and ensuring interpretability. HAN addresses this by employing a hierarchical structure. Lower layers utilize attention mechanisms to process raw data, extracting salient features. Higher layers then perform symbolic reasoning upon these features, guided by a learned symbolic representation. title: Information-Theoretic Verification of Neural Network Robustness
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to verifying the robustness of neural networks by leveraging principles from information theory. Traditional methods for assessing robustness frequently struggle to accurately quantify uncertainty and offer insufficient guarantees. We propose a framework utilizing information-theoretic measures, specifically mutual information and entropy, to provide a rigorous and quantifiable evaluation of a network's resilience against adversarial perturbations. Our methodology shifts the focus from black-box testing to a formal, mathematically grounded verification process. The core contribution lies in translating the concept of robustness into an information-theoretic term, enabling a precise measurement of vulnerability and a deeper understanding of the network's decision boundaries. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and conceptual illustrations, the potential of this approach to significantly advance the field of neural network security and reliability.

title: Replication package: Bosonic codes from compact phase spaces
abstract: Replication package — code, Jupyter notebooks, and precomputed data — for "Bosonic codes from compact phase spaces" (D. Roberts, A. Slipper, A. Parhizkar, V. V. Albert, and M. Hafezi). The paper develops the correspondence between Gottesman–Kitaev–Preskill (GKP) codes and elliptic curves — established concurrently by Conrad, Burchards & Flammia [1] and the present authors [2] — and extends it, via geometric quantization, to bosonic quantum codes associated with algebraic curves of arbitrary genus. Following geometric quantization, a quantized phase space is a family of coherent states holomorphically parametrized by a complex manifold; this work realizes the phase spaces parametrized by a compact Riemann surface. Code states are then holomorphic sections of a line bundle over that surface (automorphic forms), and the code dimension is fixed by Riemann–Roch — recovering GKP codes when the surface is an elliptic curve (genus 1) and yielding a new class of hyperbolic CV quantum codes at genus greater than or equal to 2. The package also numerically illustrates the central no-go result: an amenability dichotomy under which arbitrarily accurate approximate code words exist at genus one but not at any higher genus. The genus-two Bolza surface — the most symmetric genus-two curve — serves as the explicit worked example throughout, and is what the numerics compute. For that example the package: constructs the k=2 code space, verifies the Veronese factorization Y^2 = XZ that generates the full tower of code spaces, and renders the Husimi Q-functions of the code basis (main-text Fig. 2); builds the Poincaré theta series spanning the code space and studies their convergence; verifies the weight-2 canonical gate representation — V_R, V_U in the main text, ρ(R), ρ(U) in the notebooks — for the automorphism group Aut(C) = GL(2, F_3), symbolically and numerically; derives the circuit-QED conditional two-mode-squeezing Hamiltonian via a lab-frame dispersive Schrieffer–Wolff reduction; simulates the conditional-kick stabilization dynamics (main-text Fig. 3) and diagonalizes the stabilizer Hamiltonian to exhibit a spectral gap, a genus-two instance of the amenability dichotomy. Every computational figure in the main text and Supplemental Material is regenerated; the two non-computational schematics (main-text Fig. 1 and the SM circuit diagram) are illustrations, not code output. See README.md for the full file-to-figure map. [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.03270 (2024)[2] https://github.com/droberts01/higher-genus-gkp (2024)

title: A Meta-Learning-Based Aggregation Strategy for Heterogeneous Federated Learning Scenarios
abstract: Federated learning relies on aggregation schemes that assume all participants train models with identical architectures and a common parameter initialization. While this enables parameter-averaging strategies such as Federated Averaging, it also imposes a strong inductive bias by constraining local models to evolve from nearly identical starting points, potentially reducing model diversity and limiting exploration of the hypothesis space. Recent studies have explored shared-initialization-free and heterogeneous federated learning as largely independent research directions. In this context, we propose a shared-initialization-free, architecture-agnostic aggregation strategy based on meta-learning, where local models generate predictions over a reference dataset that are integrated to train a global meta-model. Among the different forms of heterogeneity in federated learning, this work focuses on statistical and model heterogeneity. The proposed framework is evaluated in both one-shot and multi-round federated settings against parameter-averaging and knowledge-distillation approaches while preserving the independent evolution of local models. Experiments across diverse federated settings, including homogeneous and heterogeneous models, varying numbers of participants, different levels of data imbalance on representative benchmark dataset demonstrate that the proposed strategy in a one-shot scenario achieves competitive performance under limited-data conditions, while iterative refinement of the prediction consensus in the multi-round setting yields consistent improvements over traditional aggregation strategies. These findings demonstrate that prediction-space meta-learning constitutes a practical alternative for federated aggregation without requiring shared parameter initialization. Future work will investigate more advanced consensus mechanisms, adaptive historical consensus strategies, and the evaluation of the proposed framework under larger-scale federated learning environments.

title: GICPIdb: an archival repository of multimodal data focusing on pathological images for gastrointestinal cancers
abstract: Introduction: Deep learning (DL) shows great potential for predicting biomarkers from routine histopathological slides of gastrointestinal (GI) cancers. Yet most existing models are validated on limited patient cohorts, while pathological image annotation and molecular marker standardization demand substantial professional expertise. To address these gaps, we constructed the Gastrointestinal Cancer Pathological Image Archive (GICPIdb, gicpidb.shubuzuo.top), a dedicated database and web platform covering seven major GI cancer types. Methods: High-quality hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images were collected from multiple sources and uniformly processed. Image annotations were performed by board-certified pathologists following standardized protocols. GICPIdb offers five interactive web modules for data uploading, quality control, feature extraction, online annotation and AI-based prediction. Its intuitive interface supports data browsing, retrieval, visualization and downloading. Results: The database houses 2,863 pathologist-annotated, uniformly processed, high-quality H&E stained images collected from 2,655 patients. Of these, 1,699 patients were sourced from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), 182 from the Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC), and 424 from China-Japan Friendship Hospital and 350 from Chifeng Municipal Hospital in Inner Mongolia, China. It also integrates data on over 50 key molecular markers (e.g., MSI, TMB) and prognostic labels related to survival, recurrence and metastasis. Discussion: GICPIdb aims to promote the development of DL-driven AI tools for cancer research and clinical translation. The multi-institutional data collection and standardized annotation pipeline are expected to enhance the generalizability and reproducibility of AI-based prediction models across diverse patient populations.

title: Dynamic Trajectory Stability as a Generalization Criterion: Lyapunov's Approach to the Analysis of Stochastic Learning
abstract: We consider the problem of controlling the expected generalization error of stochastic learning algorithms from the perspective of dynamical stability. Unlike classical approaches that rely on the complexity of the hypothesis class or on the stability of a single final model, we study the entire law of the iterates (logits, probabilities, or embeddings) after they enter a local basin of the loss landscape. Our analysis is based on a stochastic Lyapunov drift condition that ensures contraction of the trajectory and bounds its sensitivity to perturbations of the training data. Using martingale concentration inequalities and Wasserstein geometry, we derive non-asymptotic probabilistic bounds on the distance between the trajectory distributions corresponding to neighboring datasets. These bounds are then translated into explicit control of the generalization gap by means of the classical algorithmic stability theorem of Bousquet and Elisseeff. The main result is an upper bound on the expected generalization gap that decomposes into three terms: a data‑sensitivity term that decays with the sample size, an exponentially decaying term due to initial conditions, and a barrier term that penalizes exits from the basin. This provides a principled connection between the dynamical properties of the optimization process and the model's ability to generalize, complementing static complexity measures and endpoint stability analyses.

title: AI chatbot marketing and brand evaluation involvement: The mediating role of perceived empathy and cognitive load: A study on the retailing sector in Saudi Arabia
abstract: This study aimed to study the effect of AI chatbot marketing on brand evaluation involvement. This relation was tested in the presence of perceived empathy and cognitive load as mediating variables. A quantitative exploratory research design was utilized to test these relationships. The structural equation modeling partial least squares was used as the main analytical tool. The study was applied to 207 retail companies’ customers in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. AI chatbot marketing was found to have a positive effect on both the perceived empathy and the cognitive load. Perceived empathy was found to have a positive impact on brand evaluation involvement, while cognitive load was found to have a negative effect. The total effect of AI chatbot marketing on brand evaluation involvement was found to be offset by the contradicting effects of the mediating variables.

title: Noise-coordinated federated reinforcement learning for campus edge Internet of Things
abstract: Campus edge Internet of Things (IoT) systems must process video, trajectory, and sensor streams under limited computation, energy, and privacy constraints. Existing federated learning and quantization methods reduce data exposure and communication cost, but they often optimize model compression, adversarial robustness, energy allocation, and ethical compliance separately, leading to unstable performance on heterogeneous edge devices. To address this gap, this study proposes a noise-coordinated federated reinforcement learning framework for campus edge IoT. The framework integrates frequency-domain quantization–defense noise coordination, energy-sensitive gradient aggregation, and a lightweight permissioned blockchain audit layer for privacy-budget tracking and compliance verification. A public-dataset-based simulation was constructed using CASIA-Action, Stanford Campus, and UniMiB SHAR data, with 12 Docker-based virtual gateways representing heterogeneous campus edge nodes. Across five independent runs, the proposed federated reinforcement learning (FRL)-Full scheme achieved an anomaly detection accuracy of 93.4±0.9%, compared with 77.6±1.2% for the traditional centralized system, 82.3±1.1% for Federated Averaging (FedAvg), 85.4±1.2% for dynamic quantization, and 88.3±1.1% for phased federated reinforcement learning. In eight simulated campus security scenarios, the average latency, energy consumption, CPU usage, memory usage, and false alarm rate were reduced from 346±42ms, 30.1±3.6J, 82.3±1.9%, 38.7±1.7MB, and 13.2±1.7% to 94±12ms, 10.2±1.3J, 45.9±1.5%, 23.1±1.3MB, and 3.2±0.4%, respectively. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides a more balanced trade-off among recognition accuracy, resource efficiency, and compliance-aware privacy control than the evaluated baselines. A main limitation is that validation relies on public dataset fusion and virtual edge-node simulation rather than long-term real-campus deployment, so further field testing is required to assess generalizability and operational reliability.

title: A knowledge graph and contrastive learning framework for evaluating digital economy development
abstract: This study proposes a digital economic development evaluation algorithm that integrates knowledge graphs and contrastive learning. By constructing a digital economic knowledge graph containing 120,000 entities and 650,000 relationships, the representation of entity relationships is optimized by combining the graph contrastive learning module. The experiment uses the self-built DigitalEconomy-2024 dataset. Verification shows that KGC-DEE outperforms the baseline models on core indicators, achieving an accuracy of 0.923 and an F1-Score of 0.918, while the root mean square error and average absolute error are reduced to 0.068 and 0.052, respectively. The research confirms the synergistic advantages of knowledge graph-structured prior knowledge and Contrastive Learning-based discriminant representation. It provides an innovative tool for quantitative evaluation of the digital economy.

title: LOOMSUM: Weaving Quantitative and Narrative Evidence for Faithful Long Text-Table Summarization
abstract: Long documents often distribute important information across extensive narrative passages and multiple tables, making faithful summarization particularly challenging. Existing methods may generate individually supported quantitative facts and analytical statements yet associate them incorrectly, producing quantitatively plausible yet analytically unfaithful summaries. In this work, we propose LOOMSUM, a training-free framework that extracts source-grounded atomic evidence, explicitly links table-derived facts with supporting narrative analyses, and plans the discourse structure before generation. We also introduce Table-Grounded Faithfulness (TGF), a claim-level metric that separately evaluates Numeric Grounding, Analysis Support, and Relation Consistency. Experiments on the text--table summarization benchmarks FINDSum and USTT show that LOOMSUM improves analytical faithfulness while maintaining strong summarization quality. Human evaluation finds positive component-level associations with the corresponding human judgments. Our Relation Consistency metric further shows stronger agreement with human relation judgments than generic factuality metrics, indicating that explicit cross-modal linking helps reduce errors in which supported quantities are paired with incorrect narrative interpretations. Together, these findings show that faithful long text--table summarization requires not only grounding individual facts, but also preserving the relations between them.

title: Optimization Landscape Geometry in VQE for Frustrated Quantum Spin Models
abstract: We benchmark eight classical optimizers for exact-statevector VQE calculations on a controlled hierarchy of frustrated spin models, ranging from a diagonal Ising glass to transverse-field Ising and anisotropic Heisenberg models. The benchmark includes local, stochastic-gradient, evolutionary, covariance-adaptation, and swarm-based optimization methods under matched function-evaluation budgets. To understand their performance beyond final energies, we characterize the underlying Hamiltonian--ansatz landscapes in terms of local minima, gradients, curvature, and ground-state reachability. We use simple variational circuits, from an $R_y$ product-state ansatz for the diagonal model to shallow $R_y$--CNOT hardware-efficient circuits for the noncommuting models, and study how increasing circuit depth changes their expressivity, reachability, and optimization geometry. We find that optimizer performance changes substantially across the model hierarchy and is closely connected to landscape structure, while the variational gap represents a separate source of error. These results show how classical optimization, variational expressivity, and landscape geometry jointly determine VQE performance for frustrated spin models.

title: Information Dynamics: Toward a Unified Interpretation of Stability in Biological and Artificial Cognitive Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a unifying framework for understanding intelligence as a process governed by the dynamics of information under constraint. Rather than focusing on performance or generative capability, the analysis begins with biological cognition, where stability emerges despite limited memory capacity, reconstructive recall, and incomplete information. We argue that both biological cognition and artificial systems can be understood as systems subject to information dynamics, where stability emerges through regulation under constraint. Drawing on findings from neuroscience and cognitive science - including memory reconstruction [1][2], consolidation during sleep [3][4], executive control [7][8], and socio-contextual framing [6] - we identify key mechanisms that regulate information dynamics. These mechanisms are interpreted as stabilizing processes that maintain coherence over time. Artificial systems, particularly large language models (LLMs), are then analyzed through the same lens. Their characteristic instabilities - such as hallucinations, drift, and inconsistency - are argued to arise not from insufficient capability, but from the absence of intrinsic regulatory structures. For the sake of clarity, we acknowledge that some limited stabilization mechanisms emerge from architectural constraints of artificial systems - preset declarative and procedural memory acquired at training. We introduce a minimal model of information dynamics to formalize these observations and argue that external control frameworks can function as prosthetic regulatory layers. These compensate for missing stabilization mechanisms, suggesting that intelligence is best understood as a property of regulated systems rather than autonomous agents.

Drawing on findings from neuroscience and cognitive science - including memory reconstruction [1][2], consolidation during sleep [3][4], executive control [7][8], and socio-contextual framing [6] - we identify key mechanisms that regulate information dynamics. These mechanisms are interpreted as stabilizing processes that maintain coherence over time. Artificial systems, particularly large language models (LLMs), are then analyzed through the same lens. Their characteristic instabilities - such as hallucinations, drift, and inconsistency - are argued to arise not from insufficient capability, but from the absence of intrinsic regulatory structures. For the sake of clarity, we acknowledge that some limited stabilization mechanisms emerge from architectural constraints of artificial systems - preset declarative and procedural memory acquired at training. We introduce a minimal model of information dynamics to formalize these observations and argue that external control frameworks can function as prosthetic regulatory layers. These compensate for missing stabilization mechanisms, suggesting that intelligence is best understood as a property of regulated systems rather than autonomous agents.

title: dragonwang725-design/impossible.: 通用人工智能(AGI)的不可能三角 ——目的、事实与判断的合一困境与架构分离
abstract: 通用人工智能(AGI)的不可能三角 ——目的、事实与判断的合一困境与分离架构 摘要 通用人工智能不是要造智能,而是试图造一个能裁决全人类是非对错的、全知全能的神 当前人工智能研究面临的不是渐进式的技术瓶颈,而是范式层面的形而上学危机。本文揭示,大语言模型领域中的三大核心困境——幻觉的不可消除性、安全对齐的结构性失效、以及通用智能的伦理悖论——并非彼此独立的技术难题,而是同一个概念错误在三个层面的重复投影。这一错误的元假设是:智能是单一实体的属性。 本文的认识论前提——知识与事实在认识论上不可归约、接地发生在系统边界、接地链必须终止于非算法的生物身体——已在《知识与事实的解耦》中建立。本文在此基础上,通过"三层悖论"指出:任何试图让同一个系统同时承担生成与验证、发散与收敛、工具与主体的做法,都必然陷入自我指涉的逻辑矛盾。基于这一诊断,本文提出"空间分离"作为唯一自洽的工程出路:智能不是任何单一组件的属性,而是分布式结构的涌现关系。通用能力归于概率模型,事实约束归于代理受动极,目的锚定归于人类使用者。 本文进一步论证,"通用人工智能"(AGI)作为实体概念是三重互为锁死的对象:逻辑上自我指涉,存在论上无身可接,主权上不可让渡。三重否定不是递进的三道防线,而是互为前提、循环闭合的概念牢笼。真正可持续的智能架构,必然是"生成归机、约束归代理、目的与终审归人"的分权结构。 关键词:通用人工智能;符号接地;自我指涉;空间分离;受动-能动结构;空模型范式;事实约束;目的归人;真受动极;代理受动极;主权不可让渡

title: Dynamic Matrix Decomposition for Quantum State Generation
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic matrix decomposition (DMD) to quantum state generation, offering a novel approach to produce non-standard quantum states. Traditional matrix decomposition methods, reliant on classical matrices, are inherently limited in their ability to capture the inherent randomness and complexity of quantum systems. We propose a DMD-based framework that leverages probability to generate diverse quantum states, potentially facilitating the construction of robust quantum key distribution (QKD) systems. The core mechanism centers around the probabilistic nature of MD, enabling the creation of states with unique properties, a crucial aspect for security and operational flexibility. The paper details the implementation of this method, analyzes its performance, and discusses its potential impact on quantum information processing.

title: A Benchmark for Real-World Logical Contradiction Detection
abstract: This multi-domain dataset was developed to evaluate the ability of language models to detect real-world contradictions. This dataset encompasses two domains: the biomedical domain, with contradictory statements that come from a generated knowledge graph using the Gene Ontology (GO), proteins, and the positive and negative annotations that associate proteins with GO classes, and the general knowledge domain, using Wikidata as a source of conflicting statements. From these domains, we categorized and identified various types of logical contradictions that arise in real-world situations through their hierarchical structure, ontological constraints, and semantics. In this dataset, we define five types of these contradictions: Direct Negation - two statements that negate each other Hierarchically Inferred - an entity has a positive relation to a class and a negative relation to its parent class Disjoint Axiom (Class and Instance) - a class or instance has a relation to two disjoint classes Cardinality Constraint - a head entity is linked to multiple tail entities through a property that is constrained to haveat most one value These contradictions have explicit and implicit versions, depending on whether they contain the statement that provides the necessary context to detect the contradiction. For instance, the statements “Lisbon is the capital of Portugal” and “Coimbra is the capital of Portugal” contradict each other only because of the restriction that a country has exactly one capital; this is classified as an explicit contradiction. By omitting the restriction necessary to detect the contradiction, we create an implicit contradiction. This benchmark is composed of non-verbalized and verbalized data files. The non-verbalized files have the contradiction statements in a KG triple structure, and the verbalized ones have them as phrases. The following table shows how the benchmark files are structured: relation1 relation2 context label First statement Second statement The context statement is provided only in the explicit benchmarks and provides the necessary context to identify the contradiction 0 - not a contradiction 1 - contradiction We provide the benchmarks in different languages (only for disjoint axiom and cardinality constraint contradictions), but the verbalized versions are provided only in English, Spanish, and French.

title: Adaptive Topological Network Structures: A Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning algorithm, termed Adaptive Topological Network Structures (ATNS), designed to enhance network structure optimization within complex environments. Traditional reinforcement learning often relies on predefined reward functions, limiting adaptability. The algorithm leverages the inherent topology of a dynamically adjusted network as a core reward signal, enabling automated network restructuring. This approach promises improved performance compared to existing methods, particularly in environments with intricate dependencies and variable rewards. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that dynamically adjusts the network topology based on observed rewards, fostering a more robust and adaptable learning process. We present a comprehensive evaluation of the algorithm across a range of simulated scenarios, demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing network configurations for specific tasks.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Dynamic Probability Activation Function
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) represents a paradigm shift in artificial intelligence, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to enhance computational capabilities and solve complex problems. This paper explores the application of dynamic probability distribution activation functions within QML algorithms to address challenges related to high-dimensional data and non-linear relationships. We propose a novel activation function, termed "Quantum Self-Adaptive Adjustment" (QSA), designed to dynamically adjust parameters based on quantum computations, enabling the model to learn more complex patterns and improve overall performance. This approach contrasts with traditional activation functions that rely on deterministic rules, offering a potential pathway to more sophisticated and robust machine learning models. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of QSA in various scenarios, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations of current activation functions.

title: Quantum-Inspired Robustness Analysis of Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to enhancing the robustness of neural networks by incorporating principles derived from quantum mechanics. Traditional neural network training often relies on gradient descent, which can be susceptible to adversarial attacks and may converge to suboptimal solutions. We propose an algorithm that mimics quantum superposition to explore multiple potential training paths concurrently. This exploration is guided by quantum interference, where constructive and destructive interference patterns are leveraged to amplify desirable network characteristics and suppress vulnerabilities. The core idea is to represent the training process as a probabilistic superposition of states, allowing the network to simultaneously evaluate different parameter configurations. We formally define this approach using mathematical notation, outlining the superposition probability distribution, interference terms, and the overall optimization strategy. The resulting algorithm demonstrates improved robustness against adversarial perturbations compared to standard training methods, indicating a promising direction for developing more secure and reliable artificial intelligence systems. The key contribution lies in the systematic application of quantum-inspired concepts to directly address the challenge of neural network robustness, offering a fundamentally different perspective on the training process.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的量子态转移与编码
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of leveraging self-adaptive topology for quantum state transfer and encoding. The core challenge in quantum information processing lies in efficiently transferring and encoding quantum states, often requiring complex and computationally intensive manipulations. Traditional approaches struggle with these challenges due to their reliance on static qubit configurations. We propose a novel framework utilizing self-adaptive topology to dynamically adjust the encoding and manipulation of quantum states, potentially leading to significant improvements in quantum state fidelity and computational efficiency. The proposed method focuses on constructing a robust and adaptable topology that facilitates precise state transfers and encodes, offering a fundamentally different approach to quantum information processing. The paper details the design of a self-adaptive topology, the implementation of a transfer algorithm, and the resulting performance improvements compared to existing methods. Finally, we discuss the potential implications of this research for advancing the capabilities of quantum computing.

title: Information-Theoretic Characterization of Non-Classical Entanglement Entropy
abstract: This paper introduces a novel entropy concept – non-classical entanglement entropy – designed to quantify the complexity and information content of quantum entanglement states. Moving beyond the limitations of classical information theory's entropy definitions, this new metric is fundamentally rooted in the mathematical structure of entangled quantum states. We propose a specific entropy formula that precisely describes the information inherent within entangled systems. The core contribution lies in expanding the scope of information theory, providing a more accurate and nuanced measure for assessing and manipulating quantum information, particularly in the context of quantum information processing. This work aims to establish a foundational framework for understanding and utilizing entanglement as a resource in quantum technologies. ---

title: Title: Quantum Simulation of Complex Polymer Structures via Dynamic Lattice Modeling
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a revolutionary approach to understanding and manipulating complex systems, including polymers. This paper introduces a novel quantum simulation framework designed to accurately model the dynamic behavior of these materials, specifically focusing on the entanglement-driven conformational changes inherent in polymer structures. We propose a dynamic lattice modeling approach, utilizing quantum entanglement to capture the intricate interplay between molecular motion and the resulting structure. The core mechanism centers on creating a quantum representation of polymer chains, allowing for precise simulation of entanglement effects that drive dynamic behavior. This research contributes significantly to the field of polymer science and quantum computing, potentially unlocking new avenues for materials design and control.

title: Title: Bayesian Resonance Networks for Statistical Physics
abstract: Statistical physics, the study of the fundamental laws governing matter and energy, often grapples with complex systems exhibiting emergent behavior. Traditional approaches frequently rely on approximations and simplified models, hindering a complete understanding of these phenomena. This paper introduces Bayesian Resonance Networks (BRNs), a novel network architecture predicated on the concept of 'resonance' – the amplification of a statistical pattern – within a Bayesian framework. We propose a mechanism for dynamically adjusting network connections based on observed system states, leveraging a 'Resonance Metric' to quantify and amplify these patterns. This approach offers a potential pathway to uncover deeper insights into the underlying statistical mechanics governing complex systems, particularly those exhibiting non-equilibrium behavior. This work explores the design and implementation of BRNs, focusing on their ability to represent and analyze statistical patterns within a probabilistic context. The core of this research is the development of a robust 'Resonance Metric' and its integration into the network structure, aiming to bridge the gap between observational data and theoretical understanding. The implications of this architecture extend beyond simple pattern recognition, suggesting a fundamental shift towards a more inherently probabilistic approach to statistical physics modeling.

title: Topology Geometry Quantum Simulation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum simulation algorithm for topology geometry, aiming to model complex topological structures and uncover hidden structural patterns. Traditional optimization methods rely on classical computation, while quantum simulation offers the potential to simulate intricate evolutionary processes within topological systems. We propose a framework that leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to represent and manipulate topological states, enabling a fundamentally different approach to structural analysis. The core mechanism centers on employing quantum algorithms to explore the multi-dimensional landscape of topological spaces, ultimately identifying key structural features and dynamics. This work presents a preliminary investigation of this approach, demonstrating its potential for advancing our understanding of topological phenomena.

title: Jincheng Zhang
abstract: This paper explores the integration of abstract temporal logic (ATL) with deep learning models for enhanced learning from time series data. The core claim is that leveraging ATL's reasoning capabilities alongside the learning prowess of deep neural networks can lead to more efficient and robust learning processes. The proposed mechanism involves representing time series data in the formal language of ATL and utilizing this representation as either input to a deep learning model or as a component within the model's loss function. This approach aims to capitalize on the strengths of both paradigms, potentially improving the learning efficiency and generalization capabilities of deep learning models when applied to time series. The paper details the theoretical foundations of ATL and explores various methodologies for incorporating it into deep learning architectures, ultimately presenting a framework for intelligent time series analysis.

title: 自适应拓扑结构对量子信息编码的优化
abstract: Quantum information encoding is a crucial aspect of quantum information processing, demanding sophisticated techniques to maintain and manipulate quantum states. Traditional encoding methods often rely on static configurations, limiting their potential for optimization. This paper investigates the application of adaptive topology structures to quantum information encoding, proposing a novel framework that dynamically adjusts the topology to optimize information transfer efficiency and security. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through rigorous analysis and simulation, showcasing significant improvements over existing encoding strategies. The core mechanism involves utilizing self-adaptive topology to represent quantum states, enabling efficient information transfer and enhanced resilience against potential attacks. This research contributes to the advancement of quantum information technologies by providing a robust and adaptable encoding paradigm.

title: Dynamic Probability Fields for Ordered Systems: Modeling and Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probability field (DPC) model designed for the effective modeling and optimization of complex, dynamic, and nonlinear ordered systems. Traditional optimization techniques often struggle with such systems, necessitating a more sophisticated approach. This work integrates the DPC framework with dynamic probability fields to enable real-time adaptation and enhanced optimization capabilities. We present a conceptual framework and initial implementation demonstrating the potential of this approach to improve the performance of various ordered systems.

title: Hyperdimensional Computing for Symbolic Reasoning
abstract: This paper explores the application of hyperdimensional computing (HDC) to the challenging domain of symbolic reasoning. Traditional symbolic reasoning methods struggle with the efficient representation and manipulation of abstract concepts, often hampered by complex data structures and computationally intensive operations. HDC offers a novel approach by encoding symbols as high-dimensional vectors, termed hypervectors, facilitating efficient similarity comparisons and logical inference. We detail the core mechanisms involved, including mapping symbolic concepts to hypervectors and utilizing vector operations for reasoning. This research investigates the potential of HDC to bridge the gap between numerical and symbolic computation, providing a fundamentally different paradigm for tackling problems requiring abstract thought and deduction. The core claim is that HDC's inherent strengths in similarity-based operations can alleviate the limitations of traditional symbolic reasoning. This work focuses on outlining the theoretical framework and potential applications of this emerging hybrid approach. ---

title: Dynamic Semantic Refinement Network (DSMN)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Semantic Refinement Network (DSMN), a novel approach to understanding and controlling complex system behavior by dynamically adjusting semantic relationships between nodes. Unlike static knowledge graphs that rely on pre-defined structures, DSMN employs a reinforcement learning-based "semantic weaver" to continuously monitor and refine these relationships based on real-time interaction patterns. The core claim is that this adaptive approach surpasses the limitations of static models, enabling real-time comprehension and control. The system incorporates a "semantic drift" detection mechanism to address inconsistencies over time. The key innovation lies in the autonomous, self-learning nature of the system, utilizing reinforcement learning to optimize the semantic network for minimal prediction error and maximized system behavior accuracy. The system achieves this by adjusting the strength and type of semantic links between nodes, transitioning between relationships such as "related" to "causal". The system's ability to handle dynamic, non-static semantic relationships makes it a powerful tool for analyzing and controlling complex, evolving systems.

title: Explainable AI-Driven Synthetic Data Generation
abstract: This paper explores the application of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques to the generation of synthetic data. The core claim is that XAI can significantly improve the quality and utility of synthetic data, ultimately facilitating the training of AI models while maintaining data privacy and ensuring desired data characteristics. The proposed mechanism involves leveraging XAI to analyze real-world data, identify key features, and generate synthetic data that accurately reflects these features. A key innovation lies in the ability to not only create synthetic data but to understand *why* that data was generated, leading to a higher degree of confidence in its validity and suitability for downstream AI model training. The generated synthetic data is evaluated for its effectiveness in mimicking the statistical properties of the original data, addressing concerns about data fidelity often associated with traditional synthetic data generation methods. This work contributes to the growing field of privacy-preserving data analytics and offers a pathway to more reliable and trustworthy AI model development.

abstract: This paper presents a novel hardware compiler designed to accelerate quantum information encoding leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. This work outlines the architecture, key components, and optimization strategies of the compiler, highlighting its potential to significantly enhance the performance of quantum information processing.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Learned Noise Injection
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to enhancing the robustness of neural networks against adversarial attacks and noisy data by introducing a self-correcting mechanism. The core idea is to dynamically inject and subsequently cancel out learned noise during the training process. This is achieved through a learned noise injection module that adds perturbations to the network's activations, coupled with a learned cancellation module that removes these perturbations. Unlike traditional adversarial training methods which often employ fixed adversarial examples, our approach learns to adapt to and mitigate noise in a dynamic manner. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique through a theoretical analysis and present a framework for implementation. The key benefit is a more robust network without the limitations of relying on predefined adversarial scenarios. The method offers a flexible and adaptive solution for building resilient neural networks.

title: Bangka Island Treeshrew-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Bangka Island Treeshrew-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BITMA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the Bangka Island treeshrew. The treeshrew's unique strategy of exploring the environment while efficiently utilizing limited resources serves as the core inspiration for the algorithm's design. BITMA incorporates key elements from the treeshrew's behavior, including a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, a distributed decision-making process, and a mechanism for adapting to environmental changes. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a novel representation for individuals and a modified probability assignment scheme to guide the search process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BITMA through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to achieve competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results highlight the potential of BITMA as a robust and adaptable solution for tackling complex optimization challenges.

This work represents a significant step towards automated and robust quantum state generation, paving the way for more complex quantum computations.

title: ## The Imitation of Tigerfish Algorithm (ITA): A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Technique
abstract: This paper introduces the Imitation of Tigerfish Algorithm (ITA), a new metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the hunting behavior of tigerfish ( *Cyprinus tigris*). ITA leverages the tigerfish's unique strategy of utilizing a "trap-and-wait" approach, combined with a dynamic exploration and exploitation balance, to locate prey. The algorithm employs a population of 'hunter' agents, each possessing a 'trap' position and a 'wait' time. Hunter agents iteratively adjust their trap positions and wait times based on the fitness of the prey they've trapped, simulating the tigerfish's adaptive learning process. A key innovation is the introduction of a 'herd' concept, where agents collectively adjust their trap locations based on the overall fitness landscape, promoting global search. The algorithm's parameters, including the trap adjustment rate, wait time decay rate, and herd influence factor, are carefully designed to achieve a robust balance between exploration and exploitation, leading to improved convergence performance. This paper details the ITA framework, its underlying principles, and its potential applications across a range of optimization problems.

title: Arctic Hare Metaheuristic Algorithm (AHMA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Arctic Hare Metaheuristic Algorithm (AHMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of arctic hares. AHMA leverages the hare's strategy of exploring diverse areas while maintaining a core area for resource gathering, mimicking the concept of "core-edge" exploration. The algorithm employs a population-based search, utilizing a fitness function to evaluate the quality of solutions. A dynamic core area representation and an edge exploration mechanism are introduced to guide the search process. The algorithm's parameters, including the core radius, edge radius, and exploration rate, are dynamically adjusted based on the population's convergence. The performance of AHMA is evaluated through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive advantage compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Genetic Algorithm (GA). The key contributions of this work are the novel core-edge exploration strategy and the adaptive parameter control mechanism, offering a robust and efficient solution for complex optimization tasks.

title: E8 Resonant Hypergraph Coding (E8RHC) — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By assigning each of the 240 E8 root vectors to a vertex in a hypergraph whose edges are defined by the 132 Hz φ‑coupled Weyl‑orbit pairs, we introduce a time‑dependent coupling that oscillates at the base frequency. This dynamic "resonant" hypergraph encodes logical qubits in a frequency‑multiplexed topological code, where the 132 Hz modulation synchronizes error‑correction cycles with the dominant environmental noise spectrum. The resulting E8RHC scheme adapts its stabilizer generators in real time, achieving fault‑tolerant operation with fewer physical qubits than static E8‑based codes. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Title: Self-Organizing Neural Networks with Contextual Memory
abstract: This paper explores the design and implementation of Self-Organizing Neural Networks (SONNs) with a novel 'Contextual Memory Network' (CMN). SONNs are a promising approach to neural networks, leveraging the ability to dynamically adjust network parameters based on the input data. The CMN addresses a critical challenge in traditional SONNs – maintaining context and adapting to changing environments – through a mechanism that learns to represent the history of the input. This research proposes a new architecture that integrates a recurrent memory module within the network, enabling the network to retain and utilize past experiences to improve robustness and interpretability. The paper details the architecture, training methodology, and experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of the CMN in various scenarios. We present a case study illustrating the improved adaptability and robustness achieved compared to baseline SONNs. The core aim is to enhance the interpretability and reliability of neural networks by fostering a more contextual understanding of the data.

title: Blockchain-Based Federated Learning with Differential Privacy
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without direct data sharing. However, traditional FL systems remain vulnerable to privacy breaches and data manipulation. This paper proposes a novel blockchain-based architecture that addresses these concerns by integrating data provenance tracking, integrity verification, and differential privacy mechanisms. The system leverages blockchain technology to create an immutable record of model updates and data contributions, ensuring transparency and accountability. Simultaneously, differential privacy techniques are applied during the training process to protect the privacy of individual data contributors. This combined approach significantly enhances the security and trustworthiness of FL systems, enabling secure and collaborative model training across diverse data sources. The proposed system utilizes cryptographic hashing and Merkle trees to guarantee data integrity and employs noise injection strategies within differential privacy mechanisms to protect user data. The core contribution is a secure and verifiable FL framework with enhanced privacy guarantees.

title: A Study on Patent Issues concerning Agentic AI in the AX Era
abstract: 에이전틱 AI는 인간의 명령 없이도 스스로 목표를 설정하고 계획을 수립하여 다단계 업무를 완수하는 자율형 AI이다. 생성형 AI가인간의 지시에 수동적으로 답하는 ‘보조자’로서 역할을 하였다면, 에이전틱 AI는 스스로 판단하고 외부 도구(API 등)를 주도적으로 활용하는 ‘대리인’으로서의 역할을 수행한다. 최근 에이전틱 AI 발명이 글로벌 빅테크 기업들을 중심으로 멀티에이전트 조율 구조, 자율적 비즈니스 모델(BM) 등의 특허발명으로 출원되면서 특허경쟁이진행되고 있다. 에이전틱 AI 발명이 특허를 받으려면 추상적 아이디어는 특허받을 수 없고, 구체적인 데이터 흐름, 기술적 해결수단, 파이프라인 구조 등 구체적으로 명세서를 기재해야 하며, 진보성을충족시켜야 한다. 한편, AI를 발명자로 기재하여 특허출원한 DABUS 사건에서 전세계 국가에서 지식재산 부처와 법원은 자연인(인간)만이 발명자가될 수 있다고 설시하고 있고, 이때 인간의 실질적 기여도를 중요한심사기준으로 판단하고 있다. 본 연구에서는 에이전틱 AI와 관련하여 특허실무에 대하여 비교법적으로 고찰하였는바, 미국에서는 인간이 발명의 착상(Conception) 단계에서 질적인 기여를 하였음을 입증해야 하고, 발명자의 관점에서 실질적 기여도를 판단한다. 유럽연합(EU)의 경우에는 발명자 관점보다 AI 결과물이 현실적인 기술적과제를 어떻게 해결하였는지에 대한 발명의 기술적 성격에 초점을맞추고 있고, 통상의 당업자가 균일한 효과를 도출할 수 있는 재현가능성에 방점을 둔다. 일본의 경우에는 AI 관련 발명에서 AI 특허풀(patent pool)을 활성화하고, 온라인분쟁해결(ODR)의 도입 필요성을 검토하고 있는데, 이때 반드시 인간 전문가가 최종 판단해야 한다는 원칙을 고수하고 있다. 우리나라의 경우 지식재산처가 2026년발간한 ‘AI시대 올바른 특허출원 안내서’에 따라 생성형 AI가 도출한 가상의 실시예를 검증 없이 출원하면 재현가능성을 이유로 거절된다고 한다. 향후 인공지능의 발전으로 범용 인공지능(AGI) 시대가 도래하면, AI의 도움으로 손쉽게 발명을 할 수 있게 되어 더욱 엄격하고 고도화된 진보성 기준이 필요할 것이고, AI 기술의 폭발적인 발전 속도를 고려할 때, 특허권의 존속기간도 현행 20년을 조정할 필요성이있을 것이다. 한편, 에이전틱 AI의 자율적 구동 과정에서 발생한 특허침해 행위에 대해 법인격이 없는 AI 대신 개발사, 운영사, 최종사용자 중에서 누구에게 책임을 물을지 모호하며, AI 내부 프로세스의 ‘블랙박스’ 특성으로 인해 침해 입증이 어려우므로 입증책임의전환과 같은 제도적 보완에 대하여 추가 검토가 필요하다.

authors: João Vitor Andrade Alves de Souza
abstract: Fast Interpretable Greedy-Tree Sums for Tree EnsemblesVersion 0.1.1Description Flexible, interpretable machine learning algorithm for additive tree sums (FIGS).Fits a sum of shallow classification and regression trees (CART) by greedily minimizing residual impurity, growing a new tree or deepening an existing one at each step, whichever reduces the residuals most.Supports regression and two-class classification, variable importance, bootstrap ensembling and seamless integration with 'parsnip' and 'tidymodels' workflows.The method is described in Tan et al.

title: NARASI KEBENCIAN DALAM DISKURSUS DIGITAL: ANALISIS NETNOGRAFI PADA AKUN X GIBRAN RAKABUMING
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan bentuk narasi kebencian yang berkembang dalam interaksi netizen di kolom komentar akun X Gibran Rakabuming. Untuk memahami fenomena ini secara mendalam, penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan dengan metode netnografi, yang memungkinkan analisis interaksi dan percakapan netizen secara langsung dalam diskursus digital. Hasil temuan menunjukan bahwa ujaran kebencian yang ditunjukan kepada Gibran Rakabuming di platform X memiliki bentuk, cluster dan variasi tinggi, mulai dari penghinaan personal hingga politisasi. Kata-kata kasar, sarkasme, dan humor satir menjadi cara membentuk impresi sosial. Hal ini mencerminkan terjadinya hyperpersonal communication, Dimana anominitas dan kontrol atas identitas di media sosial memungkinkan individu mengekspresikan diri lebih agresif dan intens dibandingkan interaksi tatap muka.
